chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v01] Now the path of space is also taught, through contraction and expansion, according to the method seen in the Shaiva scriptures.

[tal-a08-v10] Rudra rules in the knot, and Isha in Maya up to the range of Sadakhya; above them is the unsupported Shiva who pervades all that, and beyond him is the supreme who pervades even that.

[tal-a08-v02] The path of time, made of the Lord's power of action, has already been examined; now the path of space, connected with the variety of forms, is being defined.

[tal-a08-v03] This entire path is established in consciousness alone; whatever does not rest there is as unreal as a flower in the sky.

[tal-a08-v04] Created through the door of consciousness, the path is situated in the void, in the intellect, in the vital airs, in the circles of channels, and also in the outer body.

[tal-a08-v05] This path should be defined in this way, because by continually attending to its proper sequence the yogi can quickly attain the state of Bhairava.

[tal-a08-v06] When, by the mere desire to see, one abides pervading all things, what more needs to be said? So it is taught in the Spanda scripture.

[tal-a08-v07] Having known the entire path, one should dissolve it into its lords, and then, as before, melt them in sequence into the circle of body, breath, and mind.

[tal-a08-v08] All of that should be dissolved into one's own consciousness; when contemplated, that consciousness, full in its own nature, becomes the fire that dissolves the ocean of worldly existence.

[tal-a08-v09] In the revered Mahikshottara, the teacher declared these lords of the path: Brahma rules from Ananta up to Pradhana, and Vishnu from Purusha up to Kala.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v11] Thus, understanding oneself as having attained Shiva-hood, it was defined in the Svacchanda teaching that this is not knowledge limited to mere procedure.

[tal-a08-v12] In the Trishiras teaching, awareness is conceived as root, middle, and tip, unfolding as the thirty-six principles, while memory is the construction of difference.

[tal-a08-v13] The root of awareness is the 'I am' state with unobstructed distinction; it is the state of all principles, present in one's own self without division.

[tal-a08-v14] The middle of awareness is marked by a certain relation of support and supported, arising through the differentiation of the principles and the standing of each in its own nature.

[tal-a08-v15] The tip of awareness is clear, waveless, and full of vast bliss; it brings beings, states, bodies, and the rest into oneness with consciousness.

[tal-a08-v16] Unbroken consciousness is Bhairava, the supreme Lord; and in the revered Deviyayamala it is said that the path is beautiful with the thirty-six principles.

[tal-a08-v17] By meditating on the sixfold path one can immediately become of the nature of Shiva, even though that Lord is not different from consciousness.

[tal-a08-v18] For the full Lord there is no real arrangement of above, beginning, middle, or end; nevertheless, such distinctions are used for the sake of those who must understand and for the one who teaches.

[tal-a08-v19] Conceptions such as middle and so forth arise according to one's own nature; therefore, by the limitation of the knower's conception, they regard the earthly principle as the lowest.

[tal-a08-v20] That principle, standing in the innermost interval of all and covered by all the envelopes, is the earthly principle; here, within that earthly principle, the arrangement of worlds is described.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v21] The ruler of the Kataha Rudras, who are devoted to desire, is Ananta; he is mounted on a vessel within the waters, reeling from drinking liquor.

[tal-a08-v22] Meditating on the god Bhairava and surrounded by serpents, he is associated with the world of Kalagni above, which rises to a height of one crore yojanas.

[tal-a08-v23] For fear of reducing the worlds to ashes, he does not look upward; and although he pervades the universe, because he burns this earth he is understood in that lower position.

[tal-a08-v24] Because he was made clear earlier in relation to the hells, he is regarded as below them; the mighty one's flame extends ten crores, and above it there is an empty space of half that extent.

[tal-a08-v25] Above that level stand the lords of hell, feeling only pain in graded order, with some in the middle and others above, surrounded by intervals of difference.

[tal-a08-v26] Among them, in order, are avici, kumbhipaka, and raurava, eleven and eleven and ten, ending at arrow-fire.

[tal-a08-v27] For each of these there is a crore height interval, a lakh measure, and a duration between sky-void mouth counts.

[tal-a08-v28] Above kushmanda, those who perform dark action contrary to scripture are placed in a lakh-less-crore station.

[tal-a08-v29] There, terrible world-persons torment them until enjoyment ends, except those who once took refuge in supreme Shiva with one-pointed mind.

[tal-a08-v30] They do not go hell-yoked; their dark result gives only small pleasure, with thousand-nine heights and one interval following in order.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v31] In the eight patalas, one each, Hatuka is lord in the eighth; Shrikantha appoints selves per world and forces many.

[tal-a08-v32] Thus that one gives powers in the raurava rule to vow-keepers and those who perform forbidden conduct.

[tal-a08-v33] Even initiated persons who lose their vow and do not perform penances become corrupters of left conduct in that place.

[tal-a08-v34] Those living by shares of god, fire, and substance stand highest; others below are devoted to garuda and other mantras.

[tal-a08-v35] They are various servants before Hatuka; but if there they worship the god-lord with devotion, they are transformed.

[tal-a08-v36] They dissolve in that lord-principle and gradually reach supreme Shiva; otherwise they remain engaged in that enjoyment.

[tal-a08-v37] They, devoted to crying under time-fire torment, dissolve in the quality-principle and then return again at creation's mouth.

[tal-a08-v38] They are cast by mothers with terrible torment into lowest-low bodies, according to their own action.

[tal-a08-v39] Among humans there, some mantra-knowers are freed in order, but others are bound according to prior deed.

[tal-a08-v40] Thus this group account, named hulahula and so on, is spoken by the blessed one in the shrimad ananda-adhika rule.

[tal-a08-v41] Above patala are thousands and twenty earth-bowl; in siddha tantra, on patala's back, it is surrounded by yakshi.

[tal-a08-v42] Adepts play with them at Bhadrakali's city; then dark hot earth, then void, then horse.

[tal-a08-v43] These are torment places for corrupters of guru-mantra and the like; then above earth and middle to Meru, thousands and sixteen.

[tal-a08-v44] Its root is submerged and spread, its height is thousand-ocean-vasu, and it is the golden abode of all gods.

[tal-a08-v45] Middle-above-below is a risen arrow-bowl square; Bhairavi and that linga are named, and earth is its pedestal.

[tal-a08-v46] All gods are indeed dissolved there; that is always worshipped in the middle, in the Meru assembly, with element and lord-direction banner.

[tal-a08-v47] Shambhu's light-peak and Shrikantha's part are that lord; descending, thousands and fourteen of Manovati.

[tal-a08-v48] Here at Meru is a four-direction circle-wall; world-guardians are placed east and south of Amaravati's center.

[tal-a08-v73] North of Kuruvarsha, in the northwest ocean, there are ten lakes in order, extending for thousands, and there are two islands, Chandra and Bhadraka.

[tal-a08-v74] On the left side of Meru stand two white-peaked mountains, and between them lies Hiranmaya, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is twelve and a half.

[tal-a08-v75] There, to the left, between the Shveta and Nila mountains, lies Ramyaka, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is twelve.

[tal-a08-v76] South of Meru are the mountains Hema and Nishadha, and between them lies Harivarsha, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is a thousand more.

[tal-a08-v77] Farther south, between Hema and Himavat, lies Kimpurusha, nine thousand in extent, where the lifespan is a thousand more.

[tal-a08-v78] South of Himavat lies Bharata, nine thousand in extent, the lowest land where beings both perform action and experience its fruits.

[tal-a08-v79] Ilavrita, Ketubhadra, Kuru, Hairanya, Ramyaka, and the regions of Hari and Kimpurusha are lands of enjoyment, but not lands of action.

[tal-a08-v80] In those regions, although they are mainly not lands of action, even animals may acquire karmic impressions because of firmly established prior conditioning.

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v81] Even beings without present impressions may appear in Bharata or elsewhere, and through firm prior impressions or by the Lord's will they may still experience good and bad results.

[tal-a08-v82] Action is also found in other places, as the ancient tradition says; there the time is always Treta, but in Bharata the full cycle of four ages prevails.

[tal-a08-v83] In Bharata there are nine divisions separated by ocean water; the land measures five hundred and the water measures five hundred as well.

[tal-a08-v84] The divisions are Indra, Kasheru, Tamrabha, Naga, eastern Gabhastimat, Saumya, Gandharva, Varaha, and the one called Kanya, extending up to the ocean.

[tal-a08-v85] In the ninth division, Kanya island, there are six sub-islands situated to the south in the middle of the ocean, and the island is adorned by seven chief mountains.

[tal-a08-v86] The mountains are Anga, Yava, Malaya, Shanku, Kumuda, and Varaha; Agastya dwells on Malaya, and Lanka stands on Trikuta—these are the six sub-islands.

[tal-a08-v87] The islands and sub-islands are inhabited mostly by various foreign peoples and are rich in pearls, gold, and gems, as stated in the teaching of Shri Ruru.

[tal-a08-v88] Whatever action is done in Bharata can be exhausted there, and by it one may reach from the lowest hell up to Shiva, or even attain liberation—especially in the region called Kanya.

[tal-a08-v89] In Bharata dwell Mahakala and a crore of Rudras, and there flow the Ganga and five hundred other sacred streams; therefore birth here is extremely hard to obtain.

[tal-a08-v90] In other regions beings pass through their karma by mere enjoyment, like animals, but for those born in Bharata even attainments beyond desire are possible.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-saṃbhavantyapyasaṃskārā bhārate@nyatra cāpi hi / dṛḍhaprāktanasaṃskārādīśecchātaḥ śubhāśubham sthānāntare@pi karmāsti dṛṣṭaṃ tacca purātane / tatra tretā sadā kālo bhārate tu caturyugam bhārate navakhaṇḍaṃ ca sāmudreṇāmbhasātra ca / sthalaṃ pañcaśatī tadvajjalaṃ ceti vibhajyate indraḥ kaśerustāmrābho nāgīyaḥ prāggabhastimān / saumyagāndharvavārāhāḥ kanyākhyaṃ cāsamudrataḥ kanyādvīpe ca navame dakṣiṇenābdhimadhyagāḥ / upadvīpāḥ ṣaṭ kulādrisaptakena vibhūṣite aṅgayavamalayaśaṅkuḥ kumudavarāhau ca malayago@gastya / tatraiva ca trikūṭe laṅkā ṣaḍamī hyupadvīpāḥ dvīpopadvīpagāḥ prāyo mlecchā nānāvidhā janāḥ / muktākāñcanaratnāḍhyā iti śrīruruśāsane bhārate yatkṛtaṃ karma kṣapitaṃ vāpyavīcitaḥ / śivāntaṃ tena muktirvā kanyākhye tu viśeṣataḥ mahākālādikā rudrakoṭiratraiva bhārate / gaṅgādipañcaśatikā janma tenātra durlabham anyavarṣeṣu paśuvad bhogātkarmātivāhanam / prāpyaṃ manorathātītamapi bhāratajanmanām

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v100] They are smeared with dirt, have long hair and beards, go naked, and behave like cows. They live for eighty years and eat grass.

[tal-a08-v91] Because Kanya island has the full variety of classes, stages of life, conduct, pleasures, and pains, it is a land of action and the supreme one.

[tal-a08-v92] Here, those who perform good and bad deeds attain the higher and lower results of heaven and hell, as stated in the Raurava-varttika.

[tal-a08-v93] Thus the region below Meru around Jambu, when described in detail, is divided into seventeen parts, but in summary into nine.

[tal-a08-v94] Svayambhuva Manu had ten sons; later three departed, and in the land called Jambu the king was Agnidhra.

[tal-a08-v95] Agnidhra had nine sons, and from them came the ninefold division; Nabhi was the ninth, and his grandson was Bharata, the son of Rishabha.

[tal-a08-v96] Bharata had eight sons and one daughter, making a ninth share; they divided and enjoyed that territory of one lakh yojanas in nine parts.

[tal-a08-v97] The salt ocean measures one hundred thousand yojanas. Outside it stand mountains, and to the north are Rishabha, Dundubhi, Dhumra, Kanka, Drona, and Indu.

[tal-a08-v98] To the west stand Varaha, Nandana, Ashoka, and Balahaka. To the south stand Chakra and Mainaka, and between those two is the submarine fire.

[tal-a08-v99] South of the ocean, two thousand yojanas away, stands the mountain Vidyutvan, three thousand yojanas high and wide. There live people who eat fruit.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-nānāvarṇāśramācārasukhaduḥkhavicitratā / kanyādvīpe yatastena karmabhūḥ seyamuttamā puṃsā sitāsitānyatra kurvatāṃ kila siddhyataḥ / parāparau svarnirayāviti rauravavārtike evaṃ meroradho jambūrabhito yaḥ sa vistarāt / syāt saptadaśadhā khaṇḍairnavabhistu samāsataḥ manoḥ svāyaṃbhuvasyāsan sutā daśa tatastrayaḥ / prāvrajannatha jambvākhye rājā yo@gnīdhranāmakaḥ tasyābhavannava sutāstato@yaṃ navakhaṇḍakaḥ / nābhiryo navamastasya naptā bharata ārṣabhiḥ tasyāṣṭau tanayāḥ sākaṃ kanyayā navamoṃ@śakaḥ / bhuktaistairnavadhā tasmāllakṣayojanamātrakāt lakṣaikamātro lavaṇastadbāhye@sya puro@drayaḥ / ṛṣabho dundubhirdhūmraḥ kaṅkadroṇendavo hyudak varāhanandanāśokāḥ paścāt sahabalāhakau / dakṣiṇa cakramainākau vāḍavo@ntastayoḥ sthitaḥ abdherdakṣiṇataḥ khākṣisahasrātikramād giriḥ / vidyutvāṃstrisahasrocchridāyāmo@tra phalāśinaḥ maladigdhā dīrghakeśaśmaśravo gosadharmakāḥ / nagnāḥ saṃvatsarāśītijīvinastṛṇabhojinaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v101] There are always unbarred doors there for entering the netherworld. This is taught by the teachers in the revered Raurava scripture.

[tal-a08-v102] Thus the salt ocean has been described. Beyond it lie six continents, and each one is surrounded by its own ocean.

[tal-a08-v103] The six continents, each successively doubled in size and ruled by six sons of Manu, are Shaka, Kusha, Krauncha, Shalmali, Gomeda, and Pushkara. Their six oceans are of milk, curd, ghee, sugarcane juice, liquor, and sweet water.

[tal-a08-v104] Medhatithi, Vapushmat, Jyotishmat, Dyutimat, King Havi, and Samvara rule Shaka and the other continents, and Agnidhra was appointed over Jambu continent.

[tal-a08-v105] The five continents beginning with Shaka are each divided into regions by seven mountains. Pushkara is divided into two parts, and there Hari, Yama, Varuna, and Indra rule in the east and the other directions.

[tal-a08-v106] From half of Meru up to the end of the sweet-water ocean, the total measure is two crores, fifty-three lakhs, and fifty thousand yojanas.

[tal-a08-v107] Beyond the seventh ocean lies a golden land extending ten crores of yojanas. After that is the Lokāloka mountain, one hundred thousand yojanas high and ten thousand yojanas broad.

[tal-a08-v108] Eight Rudras with the world-lords are stationed in the eight directions of Lokāloka. Some say the sun moves only within Lokāloka and never goes beyond it.

[tal-a08-v109] The paths of the ancestors and the gods, going south and north, are the sun's two tracks. Teachers say these are the sun's southern and northern courses.

[tal-a08-v110] Meru is north of all and Lokāloka is south. In this way one should understand the sun's rising and setting.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-niryantrāṇi sadā tatra dvārāṇi bilasiddhaye / ityetad gurubhirgītaṃ śrīmadrauravaśāsane itthaṃ ya eṣa lavaṇasamudraḥ pratipāditaḥ / tadbahiḥ ṣaḍamī dvīpāḥ pratyekaṃ svārṇavairvṛtāḥ kramadviguṇitāḥ ṣaḍbhirmanuputrairadhiṣṭhitāḥ / śākakuśakrauñcāḥ śalmaligomedhābjamiti ṣaḍdvīpāḥ / kṣīradadhisarpiraikṣavamadirāmadhurāmbukāḥ ṣaḍambudhayaḥ medhātithirvapuṣmāñjyotiṣmāndyutimatā havī rājā / saṃvara iti śākādiṣu jambudvīpe nyarūpi cāgnīdhraḥ girisaptakaparikalpitatāvatkhaṇḍāstu pañca śākādyāḥ / puṣkarasaṃjño dvidalo hariyamavaruṇendavo@tra pūrvādau tripañcāśacca lakṣāṇi dvikoṭyayutapañcakam / svādvarṇavāntaṃ mervardhādyojananāmiyaṃ pramā saptamajaladherbāhye haimī bhūḥ koṭidaśakamatha lakṣam / ucchrityā vistārādayutaṃ loketarācalaḥ kathitaḥ lokālokadigaṣṭaka saṃsthaṃ rudrāṣṭakaṃ salokeśam / kevalamityapi kecillokālokāntare ravirna bahiḥ pitṛdevapathāvasyodagdakṣiṇagau svajātpare vīthyau / bhānoruttaradakṣiṇamayanadvayametadeva kathayanti 'sarveṣāmuttaro merurlokālokaśca dakṣiṇaḥ.' udayāstamayāvitthaṃ sūryasya paribhāvayet

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v111] When it is midnight in Amaravati, it is sunset in Yama's city, midday in Varuna's city, and sunrise in Soma's city.

[tal-a08-v112] When it is sunrise in Amaravati, it is midnight in Yama's abode, sunset in Soma's city, and midday in Varuna's city. Thus the times change with the sun's movement.

[tal-a08-v113] Beyond the Lokāloka mountain lies darkness extending thirty-five hundred crores, nineteen lakhs, and forty thousand yojanas.

[tal-a08-v114] Beyond Lokāloka lies the Garbhoda ocean, the king of oceans, equal in measure to the seven oceans. In its womb rests the entire earth.

[tal-a08-v115] According to the Siddhanta scripture, on the shore of the Garbhoda ocean is a region called Kausheya. There Garuda lives surrounded by accomplished birds.

[tal-a08-v116] There they sport on mountain tops, and there are nine principal mountains. Beyond them are thirty hot-water rivers that flow down to the netherworld.

[tal-a08-v117] Then comes the Naimi garden in the four directions, always attended by yoginis. After that are Meru, the serpents, the clouds, and then the golden egg.

[tal-a08-v118] Enclosed by the shell of Brahma's egg, the world called Bhurloka extends fifty crores of yojanas in the ten directions.

[tal-a08-v119] This earth-world is filled with six kinds of beings: beasts, birds, deer, trees, humans, and reptiles. It is also inhabited by pishachas, rakshasas, gandharvas, and yakshas.

[tal-a08-v120] It is also the abode of vidyadharas, and in short, for the whole creation of beings it serves as a place of enjoyment and residence according to their desire.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ardharātro@marāvatyāṃ yāmyāyāmastameva ca / madhyandinaṃ tadvāruṇyāṃ saumye sūryodayaḥ smṛtaḥ udayo yo@marāvatyāṃ so@rdharātro yamālaye / ke@staṃ saumye ca madhyāhna itthaṃ sūryagatāgate pañcatriṃ śatkoṭisaṃkhyā lakṣāṇyekonaviṃśatiḥ / catvāriṃśatsahasrāṇi dhvāntaṃ lokācalādbahiḥ saptasāgaramānastu garbhodākhyaḥ samudrarāṭ / lokālokasya parato yadgarbhe nikhilaiva bhūḥ siddhātantre@tra garbhābdhestīre kauśeyasaṃjñitam / maṇḍalaṃ garuḍastatra siddhapakṣasamāvṛtaḥ krīḍantiṃ parvatāgre te nava cātra kulādrayaḥ / tata uṣṇodakāstriṃśannadyaḥpātālagāstataḥ caturdiṅnaimirodyānaṃ yoginīsevitaṃ sadā / tato merustato nāgā meghā hemāṇḍakaṃ tataḥ brahmaṇo@ṇḍakaṭāhena merorardhena koṭayaḥ / pañcāśadevaṃ daśasu dicu bhūrlokasaṃjñitam paśukhagamṛgatarumānuṣasarīsṛpaiḥ ṣaḍbhireṣa bhūrlokaḥ / vyāptaḥ piśācarakṣogandharvāṇāṃ sayakṣāṇām vidyābhṛtāṃ ca kiṃ vā bahunā sarvasya bhūtasargasya / abhimānato yatheṣṭaṃ bhogasthānaṃ nivāsaśca

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v121] Between bhuvarloka and the sun there are ten wind paths, each separated by ten thousand units.

[tal-a08-v122] The first wind path above is ritarddhi, fifty yojanas above.

[tal-a08-v123] The nourishing wind is followed by pracetas, higher by a hundred.

[tal-a08-v124] Mute lightning clouds stand a krosa from earth and shower rain.

[tal-a08-v125] Above them are clouds showering frogs and beings, and higher poison-water clouds.

[tal-a08-v126] Skanda-born clouds and pisacas occur in the flood wind; fifty above are maraka clouds.

[tal-a08-v127] Mahadeva-born vinayakas there take away the actions of unperfected men.

[tal-a08-v128] Fifty above is vajranka wind, with stone clouds and lowest vidyadharas.

[tal-a08-v129] Those who died with siddhi are situated in vajranka wind.

[tal-a08-v130] Fifty above vajranka are electric rain clouds, apsarasas, and merit-doing men.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-bhuvarlokastathā tvārkāllakṣamekaṃ tadantare / daśa vāyupathāste ca pratyekamayutāntarāḥ ādyo vāyupathastatra vitataḥ paricarcyate / pañcāśadyojanordhve syādṛtarddhirnāma mārutaḥ āpyāyakaḥ sa jantūnāṃ tataḥ prācetaso bhavet / pañcāśadyojanādūrdhva tasmādūrdhva śatena tu senānīvāyuratraite mūkameghāstaḍinmucaḥ / ye mahyāḥ krośamātreṇa tiṣṭhanti jalavarṣiṇaḥ tebhya ūrdhva śatānmeghā bhekādiprāṇivarṣiṇaḥ / pañcāśadūrdhvamogho@tra viṣavāripravarṣiṇaḥ meghāḥ skandodbhavāścānye piśācā oghamārute / tataḥ pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ syurmeghā mārakasaṃjñakāḥ tatra sthāne mahādevajanmānaste vināyakāḥ / ye haranti kṛtaṃ karma narāṇāmakṛtātmanām pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ vajrāṅko vāyuratropalāmbudāḥ / vidyādharādhamāścātra vajrāṅke saṃpratiṣṭhitāḥ ye vidyāpauruṣe ye ca śmaśānādiprasādhane / mṛtāstatsiddhisiddhāste vajrāṃke maruti sthitāḥ pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ vajrāṃkādvaidyuto@śanivarṣiṇaḥ / abdā apsarasaścātra ye ca puṇyakṛto narāḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v131] Those who died in these circumstances are situated in the electric level.

[tal-a08-v132] After the electric level come nourishment clouds, disease-water clouds, and samvartas.

[tal-a08-v133] In raivata there is a place for anger-water releasers, and visavarta is that wind.

[tal-a08-v134] Fifty above are storm clouds and fire-born vidyadhara specialists who worship the supreme lord.

[tal-a08-v135] A hundred above visavarta is durjaya, the breath-born.

[tal-a08-v136] Paravaha contains brahma clouds, pushkara clouds, wind-goers, and gandharvas.

[tal-a08-v137] Avaha contains jimuta clouds, highest vidyadharas, and form-vow worlds.

[tal-a08-v138] Mahavaha has beings-benefiting clouds, and mahaparivaha has skull-born clouds of mahesha.

[tal-a08-v139] At the end of mahaparivaha is ritarddhi, with eastern wind path, fire daughters, and mothers established by rudra power.

[tal-a08-v140] The second level has siddhas and caranas, the fourth has divine weapons and direction elephants, and the fifth is noted.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-bhṛgau vahnau jale ye ca saṃgrāme cānivartinaḥ / gograhe vadhyamokṣe vā mṛtāste vaidyute sthitāḥ vaidyutādraivatastāvāṃstatra puṣṭivahāmbudāḥ / ūrdhvaṃ ca rogāmbumucaḥ saṃvartāstadanantare rocanāñjanabhasmādisiddhāstatraiva raivate / krodhodakamucāṃ sthānaṃ viṣāvartaḥ sa mārutaḥ pañcāśadūrdhvaṃ tatraiva durdinābdā hutāśajāḥ / vidyādharaviśeṣāśca tathā ye parameśvaram gāndharveṇa sadārcanti viṣāvarte@tha te sthitāḥ / viṣāvartācchatādūrdhva durjayaḥ śvāsasaṃbhavaḥ brahmaṇo@tra sthitā meghāḥ pralaye vātakāriṇaḥ / puṣkarābdā vāyugamā gandharvāśca parāvahe jīmūtameghāstatsaṃjñāstathā vidyādharottamāḥ / ye ca rūpavratā lokā āvahe te pratiṣṭhitāḥ mahāvahe tvīśakṛtāḥ prajāhitakarāmbudāḥ / mahāparivahe meghāḥ kapālotthā maheśituḥ mahāparivahānto@yamṛtarddheḥ prāṅmarutpathaḥ / agnikanyā mātaraśca rudraśaktyā tvadhiṣṭhitāḥ dvitīye tatpare siddhacāraṇā nijakarmajāḥ / turye devāyudhānyaṣṭau diggajāḥ pañcame punaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v141] The sixth level has garuda, bull, and lord, with daksha; the ninth is established by brahma power.

[tal-a08-v142] The tenth wind path contains vasus, rudras, and adityas, and the sun's orb is nine thousand yojanas.

[tal-a08-v143] Svarga loka is defined from bhuvarloka to the end of dhruva, with knowledge power shining as the lord's sun.

[tal-a08-v144] Cool-rayed action power of shiva is a lakh from the sun, stellar is a lakh from the moon, then two lakhs.

[tal-a08-v145] From the earth up to Saturn, the wise know a set of five planets, each at its own interval. From the sun, the realm of the Seven Sages is one lakh away, and from there the Pole Star is placed at the same distance.

[tal-a08-v146] The unmoving Pole Star is Brahma himself in a lower form, stationed in Brahma's place. It has become the central pivot of all celestial cars and stands above them all.

[tal-a08-v147] Here, all things are understood to be bound within the sphere of wind. There are seven heavenly wind masses, chiefly beginning with the clouds and the like.

[tal-a08-v148] Those who perform sacrifices and other rites but lack knowledge go to heaven. When that merit is exhausted, they return to the human world because of the merit that still remains.

[tal-a08-v149] Thus, from the earth up to the Pole Star the distance is fifteen lakhs. From heaven up to the Great World it is two crores and eighty-five lakhs.

[tal-a08-v150] In the Great World dwell seers, sages, and perfected beings such as Markandeya. Gods whose duties have come to an end also abide there.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ṣaṣṭhe garutmānanyasmiṅgaṅgānyatra vṛṣo vibhuḥ / dakṣastu navame brahmaśaktyā samadhiti[ni]ṣṭhitaḥ daśame vasavo rudrā ādityāśca marutpathe / navayojanasāhasro vigraho@rkasya maṇḍalam triguṇaṃ jñānaśaktiḥ sā tapatyarkatayā prabhoḥ / svarlokastu bhuvarlokāddhruvāntaṃ paribhāṣyate sūryāllakṣeṇa śītāṃśuḥ kriyāśaktiḥ śivasya sā / candrāllakṣeṇa nākṣatraṃ tato lakṣadvayena tu pratyekaṃ bhaumataḥ sūryasutānte pañcakaṃ viduḥ / saurāllakṣeṇa saptarṣivargastasmāddhruvastathā brahmaivāpararūpeṇa brahmasthāne dhruvo@calaḥ / medhībhūto vimānānāṃ sarveṣāmupari dhruvaḥ atra baddhāni sarvāṇyapyūhyante@nilamaṇḍale / svassapta mārutaskandhā āmeghādyāḥ pradhānataḥ itaśca kratuhotrādi kṛtvā jñānavivarjitāḥ / svaryānti tatkṣaye lokaṃ mānuṣyaṃ puṇyaśeṣataḥ evaṃ bhūmerdhruvāntaṃ syāllakṣāṇi daśa pañca ca / dve koṭī pañca cāśītirlakṣāṇi svargato mahān mārkaṇḍādyā ṛṣimunisiddhāstatra pratiṣṭhitāḥ / nivartitādhikārāśca devā mahati saṃsthitāḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v151] In the great intermediate space there are others who still hold office. Eight crores above the Great World is the Jana world, where Kapila and others dwell.

[tal-a08-v152] Many happy Sadhyas dwell there as well. One crore above the Jana world is the Tapas world, where Sanaka and others of great wisdom reside.

[tal-a08-v153] There the lords of creatures born from Brahma hold their office. Above the Tapas world, sixteen crores away, is Satya, the abode of Brahma.

[tal-a08-v154] There the self-born Brahma dwells and manifests this universe. In the Satya world are the Vedas and others who have been refined by action and meditation.

[tal-a08-v155] There, above, one crore higher, are those established in bliss at Brahma's seat. Two crores above Brahma's seat is the city of Vishnu.

[tal-a08-v156] Devotees of Vishnu reach that abode through meditation, worship, and recitation. Seven crores above Vishnu's world is the world of the supreme lord.

[tal-a08-v157] Rudra is the maker of creation and dissolution within the cosmic egg. Those who are devoted to worship of the linga but lack initiation and knowledge are connected with his realm.

[tal-a08-v158] They go to Rudra's city within the cosmic egg and never fall back down. All who dwell there eventually go to Shiva, becoming Rudras initiated by Srikantha.

[tal-a08-v159] When their office comes to an end, they ascend together with the group of Rudra's daughters, going from city to city above Rudra in ever higher stages.

[tal-a08-v160] Below the cosmic egg and above Rudra is the city of the staff-bearer. By Shiva's will he holds the egg firm and also opens the path of liberation.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-mahāntarāle tatrānye tvadhikārabhujo janāḥ / aṣṭau koṭyo mahallokājjano@tra kapilādayaḥ tiṣṭhanti sādhyāstatraiva bahavaḥ sukhabhāginaḥ / janāttaporkakoṭyo@tra sanakādyā mahādhiyaḥ prajāpatīnāṃ tatrādhikāro brahmātmajanmanām / brahmālayastu tapasaḥ satyaḥ ṣoḍaśa koṭayaḥ tatra sthitaḥ sa svayambhūrviśvamāviṣkarotyadaḥ / satye vedāstathā cānye karmadhyānena bhāvitāḥ ānandaniṣṭhāstatrordhvekoṭirvairiñcamāsanam / brahmāsanātkoṭiyugmaṃ puraṃ viṣṇornirūpitam dhyānapūjājapairviṣṇorbhaktā gacchanti tatpadam / vaiṣṇavātsaptakoṭībhirbhuvanaṃ parameśituḥ rudrasya sṛṣṭisaṃhārakarturbrahmāṇḍavartmani / dīkṣājñānavihīnā ye liṅgārādhanatatparāḥ te yāntyaṇḍāntare raudraṃ puraṃ nādhaḥ kadācana / tatsthāḥ sarve śivaṃ yānti rudrāḥ śrīkaṇṭhadīkṣitāḥ adhikārakṣaye sākaṃ rudrakanyāgaṇena te / puraṃ puraṃ ca rudrordhvamuttarottaravṛddhitaḥ brahmāṇḍādhaśca rudrordhva daṇḍapāṇeḥ puraṃ sa ca / śivecchayā dṛṇātyaṇḍaṃ mokṣamārga karoti ca

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v161] Sharva, Rudra, Bhima, Bhava, Ugra, the great lord, and Ishana are the seven Shiva-lords of the worlds, ruling upward from the earth world.

[tal-a08-v162] Seven worlds are formed from gross particulars, while the higher worlds are formed from subtle ones. The teacher explained this clearly in the Ruru scripture.

[tal-a08-v163] In Brahma's first creation, five gross particulars called the abundant ones were made from his own body. With a seventh formed from them, these became the basis of the seven worlds.

[tal-a08-v164] Beyond that, the worlds are supported by subtle coverings: great elements born from the tanmatras, upheld through subtle bodies and mutually connected by smell and the other subtle qualities.

[tal-a08-v165] From the fire of time up to the staff-bearer the distance is eighty-eight crores. Above that, within the cosmic egg, is a solid shell one crore yojanas thick.

[tal-a08-v166] There are fifty crores above the earth's surface and fifty crores below, making the earth sphere one hundred crores in all. From that it is pictured like a golden grain of rice.

[tal-a08-v167] The mantra extending to the hundred Rudras, with the syllables hum and phat, splits that hard-to-pacify boundary. Ten by ten in every direction, there are a hundred Rudras outside.

[tal-a08-v168] That which supports the cosmic egg does so by its own power on all sides. The teachers, in the Raurava and other scriptures, have said that it has the form of an egg.

[tal-a08-v169] The cosmic egg is the mass of reality that has turned toward manifestation, emerged from the form of power, and remains undivided by any addition or removal.

[tal-a08-v170] The upper shell of the egg is sattva mixed with a trace of darkness, while the lower shell is sattva mixed with activity and associated with darkness.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śarvarudrau bhīmabhavāvugro devo mahānatha / īśāna iti bhūrlokāt sapta lokeśvarāḥ śivāḥ sthūlairviśeṣairārabdhāḥ sapta lokāḥ pare punaḥ / sūkṣmairiti guruścaiva rurau samyaṅnyarūpayat ye brahmaṇādisarge svaśarīrānnirmitāḥ prabhūtākhyāḥ / sthūlāḥ pañca viśeṣāḥ saptāmī tanmayā lokāḥ parato liṅgādhāraiḥ sūkṣmaistanmātrajairmahābhūtaiḥ / lokānāmāvaraṇairviṣṭabhya parasperaṇa gandhādyaiḥ kālāgnerdaṇḍapāṇyantamaṣṭānavatikoṭayaḥ / ata ūrdhvaṃ kaṭāho@ṇḍe sa ghanaḥ koṭiyojanam pañcāśatkoṭayaścordhvaṃ bhūpṛṣṭhādadharaṃ tathā / evaṃ koṭiśataṃ bhūḥ syāt sauvarṇastaṇḍulastataḥ śatarudrāvadhirhuphaṭ bhedayettattu duḥśamam / pratidikkaṃ daśa daśetyevaṃ rudraśataṃ bahiḥ brahmāṇḍādhārakaṃ tacca svaprabhāveṇa sarvataḥ / aṇḍasvarūpaṃ gurubhiścoktaṃ śrīrauravādiṣu vyakterabhimukhībhūtaḥ pracyutaḥ śaktirūpataḥ / āvāpavānanirbhakto vastupiṇḍo@ṇḍa ucyate tamoleśānuviddhasya kapālaṃ sattvamuttaram / rajo@nuviddhaṃ nirmṛṣṭaṃ sattvamasyādharaṃ tamaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v171] The mass of reality is said to partake of the collectivity of Shiva and Shakti, and because it turns toward manifestation it is called an egg.

[tal-a08-v172] One might object that powers immersed in Shiva should also be eggs, but they are not, because they have not fallen from their own state of power.

[tal-a08-v173] Another clarifying term is used so that egg-ness is not wrongly extended to bodies and sense bases, because nothing is inserted into them in that way.

[tal-a08-v174] If bodies and sense bases form a collectivity, their oneness is explained by the word 'undivided', which shows that they share the same kind.

[tal-a08-v175] Someone might think that, even without using the term 'mass of reality', each principle by itself could have the nature of an egg; but the text challenges that idea.

[tal-a08-v176] Egg-nature would wrongly extend to a principle made only of qualities, subtle elements, and gross elements; but the word 'reality' here means the whole made of bodies, sense bases, and worlds.

[tal-a08-v177] Because that form has already been defined, its collectivity is called an egg; and this collectivity belongs to the Lord who bears the universe as his body.

[tal-a08-v178] For that reason, other distinguishing terms were introduced, to show that egg-ness applies only within the limited states of the path-sphere that depends on Maya.

[tal-a08-v179] Others say the distinguishing terms were used to prevent egg-ness from being misapplied; in any case, beyond the Brahma egg described here there are one hundred Rudras.

[tal-a08-v180] Over those hundred Rudras stand eleven radiant Rudra-lords of their own: Ananta, Kapalin, Agni, Yama, Nairrita, Bala, and the rest named in sequence.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vastupiṇḍa iti proktaṃ śivaśaktisamūhabhāk / aṇḍaḥ syāditi tadvyaktau saṃmukhībhāva ucyate tathāpi śivamagnānāṃ śaktīnāmaṇḍatā bhavet / tadartha vākyamaparaṃ tā hi na cyutaśaktitaḥ tanvakṣādau mā prasāṅkṣīdaṇḍateti padāntaram / tanvakṣādiṣu naivāste kasyāpyāvāpanaṃ yataḥ tanvakṣasamudāyatve kathamekatvamityataḥ / anirbhakta iti proktaṃ sājātyaparidarśakam vināpi vastupiṇḍākhyapadenaikaikaśo bhavet / tattveṣvaṇḍasvabhāvatvaṃ nanvevamapi kiṃ na tat guṇatanmātrabhūtaughamaye tattve prasajyate / ucyate vastuśabdena tanvakṣabhuvanātmakam rūpamuktaṃ yatastena tatsamūho@ṇḍa ucyate / bhavecca tatsamūhatvaṃ patyurviśvavapurbhṛtaḥ tadartha bhedakānyanyānyupāttānīti darśitam / tāvanmātrāsvavasthāsu māyādhīne@dhvamaṇḍale mā bhūdaṇḍatvamityāhuranye bhedakayojanam / itthamuktaviriñcāṇḍamṛto rudrāḥ śataṃ hi yat teṣāṃ sve patayo rudrā ekādaśa mahārciṣaḥ / ananto@tha kapālyāgniryamanairṛtakau balaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v181] The remaining Rudra-lords are Shighra, Nidhisha, Vidyesha, Shambhu, and Virabhadra; they surround the Brahma egg like bees covering honey and clusters of kadamba filaments.

[tal-a08-v182] In the same way, the Shiva-Rudras, with countless attendants, surround the Brahma egg; their arrangement is described in vast numbers, such as forty niyutas and a crore.

[tal-a08-v183] Presided over by Shrikantha, these Rudras create and withdraw, and they hold lordship over the gods, as stated in the Raurava Vartika.

[tal-a08-v184] But in the Siddha Tantra, beyond a hundred crores from the golden egg, there is a sequence of a hundred more eggs, successively doubled and associated with silver and other substances.

[tal-a08-v185] In those eggs, Brahmas exist in sequence with doubled lifespans; they perish in order, and at the end of that series a higher principle is reached.

[tal-a08-v186] From earth upward come water and the rest in order; up to ego the scale increases tenfold, and beyond that intellect increases a hundredfold.

[tal-a08-v187] Above intellect, manifest nature is a thousandfold, purusha is ten thousandfold, and niyati is a hundred thousandfold, leading to a millionfold beyond it.

[tal-a08-v188] Up to kala the scale is ten millionfold, Maya is a hundred millionfold, Ishvara is a billionfold, and beyond that it reaches a thousand crores.

[tal-a08-v189] Sadakhya pervades at that vast scale, and together with its multitude of powers the all-pervading goddess is established as pervading the entire path.

[tal-a08-v190] Beyond all that is the pure, supreme, immeasurable Shiva principle; from water up to Shiva-tattva, no one but Shiva has truly seen it.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śīghro nidhīśo vidyeśaḥ śambhuḥ savīrabhadrakaḥ / madhu madhukṛtaḥ kadambaṃ kesarajālāni yadvadāvṛṇate tadvatte śivarudrā brahmāṇḍamasaṃkhyaparivārāḥ / śarāṣṭaniyutaṃ koṭirityeṣāṃ sanniveśanam śrīkaṇṭhādhiṣṭhitāste ca sṛjanti saṃharanti ca / īśvaratvaṃ diviṣadāmiti rauravavārtike siddhātantre tu hemāṇḍācchatakoṭerbahiḥ śatam / aṇḍānāṃ kramaśo dvidviguṇaṃ rūpyādiyojitam teṣu krameṇa brahmāṇaḥ saṃsyurdviguṇajīvitāḥ / kṣīyante kramaśaste ca tadante tattvamammayam dharāto@tra jalādi syāduttarottarataḥ kramāt / daśadhāhaṅkṛtāntaṃ dhīstasyāḥ syācchatadhā tataḥ sahasradhā vyaktamataḥ pauṃsnaṃ daśasahasradhā / niyatirlakṣadhā tasmāttasyāstu daśalakṣadhā kalāntaṃ koṭidhā tasmānmāyā viddaśakoṭidhā / īśvaraḥ śatakoṭiḥ syāttasmātkoṭisahasradhā sādākhyaṃ vyaśnute tacca śaktirvṛndena saṃkhyayā / vyāpinī sarvamadhvānaṃ vyāpyadevī vyavasthitā aprameyaṃ tataḥ śuddhaṃ śivatattvaṃ paraṃ viduḥ / jalādeḥ śivatattvāntaṃ na dṛṣṭaṃ kenacicchivāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v191] For that reason, knowledge of Shiva is the supreme cause of liberation, as Mahadeva declares in the revered Svacchanda scripture.

[tal-a08-v192] A bound soul does not attain liberation by hundreds of other kinds of knowledge; knowledge of Shiva does not arise without receiving Shaiva initiation.

[tal-a08-v193] The former supreme power, and the human-made one too, again grants blue-radiant victory above the hundred rudras, associated with Bhadrakali.

[tal-a08-v194] Kali's victorious city is not attainable by sacrifice, gift, or austerity; her devotees, well initiated in her circle, go there.

[tal-a08-v195] The supreme goddess gives liberation through seedless initiation; she performs for people as much initiation as corresponds to the vidyesha veil.

[tal-a08-v196] Those placed in this world attain a corresponding state; then Virabhadra, shining like end-of-age fire, appears by crores.

[tal-a08-v197] Those who remember the great lord and die in water, desert, fire, or by beheading reach his city called Vijaya.

[tal-a08-v198] They go to knowledge-Ishana and radiant Virabhadra, in a region spread by crores above Virabhadra, in three ways.

[tal-a08-v199] The water-bearing rudra egg, bow-shaped, is situated from Virabhadra's world and likewise from Bhadrakali's abode.

[tal-a08-v200] Adorned by thirteen other worlds, then earth with its mountain is defined by holding the smell tanmatra.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ṛte tataḥ śivajñānaṃ paramaṃ mokṣakāraṇam / tathā cāha mahādevaḥ śrīmatsvacchandaśāsane nānyathā mokṣamāyāti paśurjñānaśatairapi / śivajñānaṃ na bhavati dīkṣāmaprāpya śāṅkarīm prāktanī pārameśī sā pauruṣeyī ca sā punaḥ / śatarudrordhvato bhadrakālyā nīlaprabhaṃ jayam na yajñadānatapasā prāpyaṃ kālyāḥ puraṃ jayam / tadbhaktāstatra gacchanti tanmaṇḍalasudīkṣitāḥ nirbījadīkṣayā mokṣaṃ dadāti parameśvarī / vidyeśāvaraṇe dīkṣāṃ yāvatīṃ kurute nṛṇām tāvatīṃ gatimāyānti bhuvane@tra niveśitāḥ / tataḥ koṭyā vīrabhadro yugāntāgnisamaprabhaḥ vijayākhyaṃ puraṃ cāsya ye smaranto maheśvaram / jaleṣu maruṣu cāgnau śiraśchedena vā mṛtāḥ te yānti bodhamaiśānaṃ vīrabhadraṃ mahādyutim / vairabhadrordhvataḥ koṭirviṣkambhādvistṛtaṃ tridhā rudrāṇḍaṃ sālilaṃ tvaṇḍaṃ śakracāpākṛti sthitam / ā vīrabhadrabhuvanādbhadrakālyālayāttathā trayodaśabhiranyaiśca bhuvanairupaśobhitam / tato bhuvaḥ sahādreḥ pūrgandhatanmātradhāraṇāt

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v201] The dead go to that supreme earth; the wise go to the ocean city, attainable by holding the taste tanmatra.

[tal-a08-v202] Then Shri's city is reached in Rudra's play descents, especially by special death at Prayaga and Shri mountain.

[tal-a08-v203] Sarasvati city is the abode of knowers of sound-Brahman; those suitable to Rudra are situated there, while others stand apart from Rudras due to primacy.

[tal-a08-v204] In many cities Ganga, Shri, and Sarasvati appear; god-lords range from Lakula to Amarasha, with eight in the waters.

[tal-a08-v205] Then the fiery principle is the abode of Shiva-fire here; those who have resorted to fiery holding go to this fire.

[tal-a08-v206] In the fiery principle there are eight leaders from Bhairava to Hari; breath has a world, and air is divided in ten ways.

[tal-a08-v207] Having meditated or abandoned breaths and made holding there, great souls enter that, becoming air and sky-bodied.

[tal-a08-v208] The eight from Bhima to Gaya go to the air principle; the sky world is attainable by holding that space.

[tal-a08-v209] From cloth-foot-end to pillar-etc and eight gods are in the space principle; uninitiated beings claiming the Shiva principle are among beings.

[tal-a08-v210] Even those lacking knowledge, despite strong holding, go outside from the egg; earth, ocean, fire, air, and space goers, and initiated ones too, are named.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-mṛtā gacchanti tāṃ bhūmiṃ dharitryāḥ paramāṃ budhāḥ / abdheḥ puraṃ tatastvāpyaṃ rasatanmātradhāraṇāt tataḥ śriyaḥ puraṃ rudrakrīḍāvataraṇeṣvatha / prayāgādau śrīgirau ca viśeṣānmaraṇena tat sārasvataṃ puraṃ tasmācchabdabrahmavidāṃ padam / rudrocitāstā mukhyatvādrudrebhyo@nyāstathā sthitāḥ pureṣu bahudhā gaṅgā devādau śrīḥ sarasvatī / lakulādyamareśāntā aṣṭāvapsu surādhipāḥ tatastu taijasaṃ tattvaṃ śivāgneratra saṃsthitiḥ / te cainaṃ vahnimāyānti vāhnīṃ ye dhāraṇāṃ śritāḥ bhairavādiharīndvantaṃ taijase nāyakāṣṭakam / prāṇasya bhuvanaṃ vāyordaśadhā daśadhā tu tat dhyātvā tyaktvātha vā prāṇān kṛtvā tatraiva dhāraṇām / taṃ viśanti mahātmāno vāyubhūtāḥ khamūrtayaḥ bhīmādigayaparyantamaṣṭakaṃ vāyutattvagam / khatattve bhuvanaṃ vyomnaḥ prāpyaṃ tadvyomadhāraṇāt vastrāpadāntaṃ sthāṇvādi vyomatattve surāṣṭakam / adīkṣitā ye bhūteṣu śivatattvābhimāninaḥ jñānahīnā api prauḍhadhāraṇāste@ṇḍato bahiḥ / dharābdhitejo@nilakhapuragā dīkṣitāśca vā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v211] For the purpose of purification yoga, the supreme state is not sought in such descents, even for those who die in shrines.

[tal-a08-v212] Having attained that state, they gradually go to Shiva-nature; this is said again in the Shrimad Devi Tantra.

[tal-a08-v213] In the Shri Kamika's Kashmir description the lord has said that those who die in the great abode of the goddess die in that city.

[tal-a08-v214] Brahmins and mixed castes, beings up to immobile forms, and Rudra classes are these; thus says Lord Shiva.

[tal-a08-v215] Dear one, the cities of tanmatras through mind lie above the sky veil and below ego, in Shiva's doctrine.

[tal-a08-v216] The great smell-tanmatra circle, joined with five colors, is situated between, covered by many crores of yojanas.

[tal-a08-v217] Thus the circles of measures beginning with essence, each by its own color, are Śarva, Bhava, Paśupati, Īśa, and Bhīma in order.

[tal-a08-v218] The lords of the tanmatras—sound and the rest—are the makers of space and the other elements; by whose will they act, from that arise the spheres of the sun, moon, and Vedas, through the great all-pervading one.

[tal-a08-v219] Among these, ugra and the rest; lords from them, sun and moon; together with sacrificers—thus eight supreme forms of Śambhu are declared.

[tal-a08-v220] The other worlds in Brahma's egg, having pervaded all, are situated; in each eon they are indeed produced from earth and the rest.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tāvatsaṃskārayogārthaṃ na paraṃ padamīhitum / tathāvidhāvatāreṣu mṛtāścāyataneṣu ye tatpadaṃ te samāsādya kramādyānti śivātmatām / punaḥ punaridaṃ coktaṃ śrīmaddevyākhyayāmale śrīkāmikāyāṃ kaśmīravarṇane coktavānvibhuḥ / sureśvarīmahādhāmni ye mriyante ca tatpure brāhmaṇādyāḥ saṅkarāntāḥ paśavaḥ sthāvarāntagāḥ / rudrajātaya evaite ityāha bhagavāñchivaḥ ākāśāvaraṇādūrdhvamahaṅkārādadhaḥ priye / tanmātrādimano@ntānāṃ purāṇi śivaśāsane pañcavarṇayutaṃ gandhatanmātramaṇḍalaṃ mahat / ācchādya yojanānekakoṭibhiḥ sthitamantarā evaṃ rasādimātrāṇāṃ maṇḍalāni svavarṇata / śarvo bhavaḥ paśupatirīśo bhīma iti kramāt tanmātreśā yadicchātaḥ śabdādyāḥ khādikāriṇaḥ / tataḥ sūryenduvedānāṃ maṇḍalāni vibhurmahān ugraścetyeṣu patayastebhyo@rkendū sayājakau / ityaṣṭau tanavaḥ śaṃbhoryāḥ parāḥ parikīrtitāḥ aparā brahmaṇo@ṇḍe tā vyāpya sarvaṃ vyavasthitāḥ / kalpe kalpe prasūyante dharādyāstābhya eva tu

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v221] Then the group of organs, joined with the speech and action senses, has Agni, Indra, Viṣṇu, and Mitra as leaders, with Brahmā among them.

[tal-a08-v222] From that heard light-circle, the intellect and the five senses have as their deities directions, lightning, sun, Varuṇa, and earths; ear and the rest likewise.

[tal-a08-v223] Above the sphere of light is situated the sphere of the five objects; from this, the sphere of mind is presided over by Soma, because...

[tal-a08-v224] Presiding over the external gods, whose nature is equality, sovereignty, and bliss, the mind-god is then declared to be the divine, all-pervading Soma.

[tal-a08-v225] Then also, the world-city of the ego-principle is joined with all sense-organs, arising from the source born of intellect-senses, together with eight from gross to goat.

[tal-a08-v226] The buddhi-principle; then the lord of the eight divine-womb cities, from paiśāca up to brāhma, is declared.

[tal-a08-v227] These are indeed the ancient abodes of the divine wombs; having descended and meditated on their own birth, they arise.

[tal-a08-v228] By the command of the supreme lord, beings are impelled by māyā and regulated by niyati, in connection with Brahmā's unmanifest birth.

[tal-a08-v229] Therefore, at the beginning of creation, the great beings are manifested in many names and forms through their own aspect, yet they do not abandon their own abode.

[tal-a08-v230] And it was said to us by a teacher established in authority and knowing the Shiva doctrine that these are indeed the wombs of manifestation of power for the eight gods.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tato vāgādikarmākṣayuktaṃ karaṇamaṇḍalam / agnīndraviṣṇumitrāḥ sabrahmāṇasteṣu nāyakāḥ prakāśamaṇḍalaṃ tasmācchrutaṃ buddhyakṣapañcakam / digvidyudarkavaruṇabhuvaḥ śrotrādidevatāḥ prakāśamaṇḍalādūrdhvaṃ sthitaṃ pañcārthamaṇḍalam / manomaṇḍalametasmāt somenādhiṣṭhitaṃ yataḥ bāhyadeveṣvadhiṣṭhātā sāmyaiśvaryasukhātmakaḥ / manodevastato divyaḥ somo vibhurudīritaḥ tato@pi sakalākṣāṇāṃ yonerbuddhyakṣajanmanaḥ / sthūlādicchagalāntāṣṭayuktaṃ cāhaṅkṛteḥ puram buddhitattvaṃ tato devayonyaṣṭakapurādhipam / paiśācaprabhṛtibrāhmaparyantaṃ tacca kīrtitam etāni devayonīnāṃ sthānānyeva purāṇyataḥ / avatīryātmajanmānaṃ dhyāyantaḥ saṃbhavanti te parameśaniyogācca codyamānāśca māyayā / niyāmitā niyatyā ca brahmaṇo@vyaktajanmanaḥ vyajyante tena sargādau nāmarūpairanekadhā / svāṃśanaiva mahātmāno na tyajanti svaketanam uktaṃ ca śivatanāvidamadhikārapadasthitena guruṇā naḥ / aṣṭānāṃ devānāṃ śaktyāvirbhāvayonayo hyetāḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v231] Below these, their bodily enjoyments are declared to be abundant, and there are forty worlds with corresponding regions of equal enjoyment.

[tal-a08-v232] These are described only as groups of eight and five because of differences in means, and they are reached through devotion, yoga, the giving up of life, and so forth.

[tal-a08-v233] Among these, Umapati alone is the lord, possessing independent senses yet being without organs; from him, by gradation, the octad of divine wombs is to be recognized.

[tal-a08-v234] The senses of the worlds are instruments that delimit objects; through a sequence increasing by one from smell up to mahat, sovereignty arises.

[tal-a08-v235] Knowing thus that powers like anima operate in this range from the paisaca level up to Virinca, one should purify the intellect together with the eight constituents of the subtle city and the senses.

[tal-a08-v236] They know the octad of Krodhesas, beginning with Samvarta and led by Anila, and then the octad of fires arising from the wrathful octad beginning with Baladhyaksa.

[tal-a08-v237] Then the octad of yogas beginning with Akrta is declared in the intellect in the Svacchanda teaching, but in the teaching beginning with Sri it is placed in the root.

[tal-a08-v238] At the level of the yoga octad, in Soma, there is what belongs to Srikantha; then comes the city of Maya, which is again spoken of as belonging to Srikantha.

[tal-a08-v239] Therefore, a second world is spoken of separately for those two; there, in the city of Maya, the universe is presided over by a goddess.

[tal-a08-v240] In each cosmic age that great goddess is described by different names; the city of the lord of Uma is then surrounded by the Mothers.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tanubhogāḥ punareṣāmadhaḥ prabhūtātmakāḥ proktāḥ / catvāriṃśattulyopabhogadeśādhikāni bhuvanāni sādhanabhedātkevalamaṣṭakapañcakatayoktāni / etāni bhaktiyogaprāṇatyāgādigamyāni teṣūmāpatireva prabhuḥ svatantrendriyo vikaraṇātmā / taratamayogena tato@pi devayonyaṣṭakaṃ lakṣyaṃ tu lokānāmakṣāṇi ca viṣayaparicchittikaraṇāni / gandhādermahadantādekādhikyena jātamaiśvaryam aṇimādyātmakamasminpaiśācādye viriñcānte / jñātvaivaṃ śodhayedbuddhiṃ sārdhaṃ puryaṣṭakendriyaiḥ krodheśāṣṭakamānīlaṃ saṃvartādyaṃ tato viduḥ / tejoṣṭakaṃ balādhyakṣaprabhṛtikrodhanāṣtakāt akṛtādi tato buddhau yogāṣṭakamudāhṛtam / svacchandaśāsane tattu mūle śrīpūrvaśāsane yogāṣṭakapade yattu some śraikaṇṭhameva ca / tato māyāpuraṃ bhūyaḥ śrīkaṇṭhasya ca kathyate tena dvitīyaṃ bhuvanaṃ tayoḥ pratyekamucyate / tatra māyāpuraṃ devyā yayā viśvamadhiṣṭhitam pratikalpaṃ nāmabhedairbhaṇyate sā maheśvarī / umāpateḥ puraṃ paścānmātṛbhiḥ parivāritam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v241] Shrikantha is the supreme form, and attendant goddesses such as Brahmi, Skandaja, Hari, Varahi, Indri, Viccika, and Carcika are named.

[tal-a08-v242] Yellow, white, yellow-blue, blue, and white-red are assigned in order to the corresponding directional goddesses.

[tal-a08-v243] By portion, the creator descends some goddesses into the human world, while other supreme ones remain established in the sky.

[tal-a08-v244] Those goddesses serve self-willed, because above the city of Uma's lord stands the supreme eight-fold form.

[tal-a08-v245] From those whose creation begins with Sharva and earth, the Ishana form is established on Meru.

[tal-a08-v246] Shrikantha pervades the world through eight bodies, and restrained devotees worship Shambhu's qualified yoga.

[tal-a08-v247] By seeing that circle, one is freed from duality, the three are removed, and the gunas are established in purity and impurity.

[tal-a08-v248] Because of gradation and difference in yoga, the fruits are varied, and this difference is called difference in enjoyment and attainment.

[tal-a08-v249] Above the eight forms, twelve radiant saffron forms are declared, ranging from Vama to Eka Shiva.

[tal-a08-v250] Above that stands Virabhadra, lord of the circle; one who attains sayujya delights together with him.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śrīkaṇṭha eva parayā mūrtyomāpatirucyate / brāhmyaiśī skandajā hārī vārāhyaindrī saviccikā [carcikā] pītā śuklā pītanīle nīlā śuklāruṇā kramāt / agnīśasaumyayāmyāpyapūrvanairṛtagāstu tāḥ aṃśena mānuṣe loke dhātrā tā hyavatāritāḥ / svacchandāstāḥ parāścānyāḥ pare vyomni vyavasthitāḥ svacchandaṃ tā niṣevante saptadheyamumā yataḥ / umāpatipurasyordhva sthitaṃ mūrtyaṣṭakaṃ param śarvādikaṃ yasya sṛṣṭirdharādyā yājakāntataḥ / tābhya īśānamūrtiryā sā merau saṃpratiṣṭhitā śrīkaṇṭhaḥ sphaṭikādrau sā vyāptā tanvaṣṭakairjagat / ye yogaṃ saguṇaṃ śambhoḥ saṃyatāḥ paryupāsate tanmaṇḍalaṃ vā dṛṣṭvaiva muktadvaitā hṛtatrayāḥ / guṇānāmādharauttaryācchuddhāśuddhatvasaṃsthiteḥ tāratamyācca yogasya bhedātphalavicitratā / tato bhogaphalāvāptibhedādbhedo@yamucyate mūrtyaṣṭakopariṣṭāttu suśivā dvādaśoditāḥ / vāmādyekaśivāntāste kuṅkumābhāḥ sutejasaḥ tadūrdhva vīrabhadrākhyo maṇḍalādhipatiḥ sthitaḥ / yatta [sta] tsāyujyamāpannaḥ sa tena saha modate

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v251] From the eight divine wombs to the thumb-sized end, eight Mahadevas may be, and this intellect principle is declared.

[tal-a08-v252] At the end of the eight Mahadevas, the eight yoga is declared here; there Shrikantha, lord of Uma, is declared.

[tal-a08-v253] Auspicious forms, the hero, the eight Mahadevas, and the body are named; nature's gunas are above and below intellect.

[tal-a08-v254] There agitated gunas produce intellect; inequality not attained is not a cause for producing effects.

[tal-a08-v255] Nature may be cause through guna equilibrium, but without agitation it still has unequal gunas.

[tal-a08-v256] How would instability arise in the first agitation? This is Sankhya's fault, if by that those gunas.

[tal-a08-v257] The unmanifest is desired; equilibrium is mere contact, not otherwise, and our view joins it with the independent lord's will agitation.

[tal-a08-v258] The unmanifest is cause of intellect principle; agitated gunas are involved, and nature's agitation comes from the lord's will before.

[tal-a08-v259] That indeed may be the intellect principle; what need of other imagined gunas? It is not obstructed by cause-form reflection.

[tal-a08-v260] Then other agitation produces effects like seed and sprout, and rows of heavy ones are established in tamas, rajas, and sattva.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tato@pyaṅguṣṭhamātrāntaṃ mahādevāṣṭakaṃ bhavet / buddhitattvamidaṃ proktaṃ devayonyaṣṭakāditaḥ mahādevāṣṭakānte tad yogāṣṭakamihoditam / tatra śraikaṇṭhamuktaṃ yat tasyaivomāpatistathā mūrtayaḥ suśivā vīro mahādevāṣṭakaṃ vapuḥ / upariṣṭāddhiyo@dhaśca prakṛterguṇasaṃjñitam tattvaṃ tatra tu saṃkṣubdhā guṇāḥ prasuvate dhiyam / na vaiṣamyamanāpannaṃ kāraṇaṃ kāryasūtaye guṇasāmyatmikā tena prakṛtiḥ kāraṇaṃ bhavet / nanvevaṃ sāpi saṃkṣobhaṃ vinā tānviṣamānguṇān kathaṃ suvīta tatrādye kṣobhe syādanavasthitiḥ / sāṃkhyasya doṣa evāyaṃ yadi vā tena te guṇāḥ avyaktamiṣṭāḥ sāmyaṃ tu saṅgamātraṃ na cetarat / asmākaṃ tu svatantreśatathecchākṣobhasaṃgatam avyaktaṃ buddhitattvasya kāraṇaṃ kṣobhitā guṇāḥ / nanu tattveśvarecchāto yaḥ kṣobhaḥ prakṛteḥ purā tadeva buddhitattvaṃ syāt kimanyaiḥ kalpitairguṇaiḥ / naitatkāraṇatārūpaparāmarśāvarodhi yat kṣobhāntaraṃ tataḥ kārya bījocchūnāṅkurādivat / kramāttamorajaḥsattve gurūṇāṃ paṅktayaḥ sthitāḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v261] Three, thirty-two, one, thirty-one, and twenty-one are listed; by their own knowledge, yoga, and power, the best teachers play.

[tal-a08-v262] Three-eyed ones, freed from bonds, do grace; intellect and guna extend to both, seven more than a hundred.

[tal-a08-v263] Among Rudras and worlds, chiefly others, the eight yoga is declared between them, in the guna mass and again in Shiva's body.

[tal-a08-v264] Having transcended the womb, in the secondary mass, yoga givers would be unmade, made, vibhu, Virincha, Hari, Guha, and then goddess by order.

[tal-a08-v265] From the unmanifest arise the organs, the subtle powers like smallness, the effects, the manifold of cognitions, and the qualities beginning with sattva.

[tal-a08-v266] These givers of yoga, arising from the qualities, bestow on souls merit, knowledge, dispassion, lordship, and their various fruits.

[tal-a08-v267] Beyond them is the world of the god Śrīkaṇṭhanātha, who is seated on the qualities beginning with sattva and is the lord and consort of the one mother of the entire universe.

[tal-a08-v268] By his power, taking a seizing form, he presides over the beings in the worlds of Umā, Guha, Nīla, Brahmā, Ṛbhukṣa, Kṛta, Akṛta, and others.

[tal-a08-v269] When he wishes to withdraw the worlds, he enters the lotus of the four-faced Brahmā, burns the four worlds, and then creates the human worlds again.

[tal-a08-v270] By his will, Rudrāṇī, whose body consists of the qualities beginning with sattva, brings forth in each cycle, and there she is worshiped at the altar in every cycle.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tisro dvātriṃśadekātastriṃśadapyekaviṃśatiḥ / svajñanayogabalataḥ krīḍanto daiśikottamāḥ trinetrāḥ pāśanirmuktāste@trānugrahakāriṇaḥ / buddheśca guṇaparyantamubhe saptādhike śate rudrāṇāṃ bhuvanānāṃ ca mukhyato@nye tadantare / yogāṣṭakaṃ guṇaskandhe proktaṃ śivatanau punaḥ yonīratītya gauṇe skandhe syuryogadātāraḥ / akṛtakṛtavibhuviriñcā harirguhaḥ kramavaśāttato devī karaṇānyaṇimādiguṇāḥ kāryāṇi pratyayaprapañcaśca / avyaktādutpannā guṇāśca sattvādayo@mīṣām dharmajñānavirāgānaiśvaryaṃ tatphalāni vividhāni / yacchanti guṇebhyo@mī puruṣebhyo yogadātāraḥ tebhyaḥ parato bhuvanaṃ sattvādiguṇāsanasya devasya / sakalajagadekamāturbhartuḥ śrīkaṇṭhanāthasya yenomāguhanīlabrahmaṛbhukṣakṛtākṛtādibhuvaneṣu / graharūpiṇyā śaktyā prābhvyādhiṣṭhāni bhūtāni upasaṃjihīrṣuriha yaścaturānanapaṅkajaṃ samāviśya / dagdhvā caturo lokāñjanalokānnirmiṇoti punaḥ yasyecchātaḥ sattvādiguṇaśarīrā visṛjati rudrāṇī / anukalpo rudrāṇyā vedī tatrejyate@nukalpena

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v271] Then, in connection with that attainment, Paśupati, Indra, Upendra, Viriñci, the gods, and also gandharvas, yakṣas, rākṣasas, ancestors, and sages perform varied sacrifices.

[tal-a08-v272] The supreme equilibrium of the qualities is the unmanifest. Above the level of the qualities are Krodheśa, Caṇḍa, Saṃvarta, Jyotiḥ, Piṅgala, and Sūraka.

[tal-a08-v273] There are Pañcāntaka, Ekavīra, and Śikhin, making eight. There that principle is the dense resting place of the soul, prakṛti, the root, pradhāna, the unmanifest.

[tal-a08-v274] These are synonymous names for the cause of the qualities, belonging to what arises from māyā; all the embodied knowers whose minds are stained by innate and adventitious impurity are there.

[tal-a08-v275] All of them are established there, along with Rudras who enjoy the experiences arising from it. Some have faculties that are deluded, manifest, or dissolved, while others are without faculties.

[tal-a08-v276] In the teaching, faculties that are not yet governed and cannot act are called deluded, while those that clearly grasp their fixed objects are called unfolded.

[tal-a08-v277] At the great dissolution they are broken and dissolved; at creation they are not yet produced. Dependent on will, they are again called without faculties, and the same is true of their effects.

[tal-a08-v278] At the level of the puruṣa principle there are the nine satisfactions, the eight accomplishments, and likewise the eight worlds beginning with aṇimā.

[tal-a08-v279] When what is not the true principle is taken as a principle, the resulting contentment is called satisfaction. Taking what should be rejected as acceptable is called accomplishment, as the Kāpilas say.

[tal-a08-v280] Four satisfactions are internal, named prakṛti, acquisition, time, and fortune. Five arise from turning away from objects through gain, protection, association, loss, and obstruction.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-paśupatirindropendraviriñcairatha tadupalambhato devaiḥ / gandharvayakṣarākṣasapitṛmunibhiścitritāstathā yāgāḥ guṇānāṃ yatparaṃ sāmyaṃ tadavyaktaṃ guṇordhvataḥ / krodheśacaṇḍasaṃvartā jyotiḥpiṅgalasūrakau pañcāntakaikavīrau ca śikhodaścāṣṭa tatra te / gahanaṃ puruṣanidhānaṃ prakṛtirmūlaṃ pradhānamavyaktam guṇakāraṇamityete māyāprabhavasya paryāyāḥ / yāvantaḥ kṣetrajñāḥ sahajāgantukamalopadigdhacitaḥ te sarve@tra vinihitā rudrāśca tadutthabhogabhujaḥ / mūḍhavivṛttavilīnaiḥ karaṇaiḥ kecittu vikaraṇakāḥ akṛtādhiṣṭhānatayā kṛtyāśaktāni mūḍhāni / pratiniyataviṣayabhāñji sphuṭāni śāstre vivṛttāni bhagnāni mahāpralaye sṛṣṭau notpāditāni līnāni / icchādhīnāni punarvikaraṇasaṃjñāni kāryamapyevam puṃstattve tuṣṭinavakaṃ siddhayo@ṣṭau ca tatpuraḥ / tāvatya evāṇimādibhuvanāṣṭakameva ca atattve tattvabuddhyā yaḥ santoṣastuṣṭiratra sā / heye@pyādeyadhīḥ siddhiḥ tathā coktaṃ hi kāpilaiḥ ādhyātmikāścatasraḥ prakṛtyupādānakālabhāgyākhyāḥ / pañca viṣayoparamato@rjanarakṣāsaṅgasaṃkṣayavighātaiḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v281] Reasoning, scriptural word, and study are three means that remove suffering; gaining friends and giving are also included, making the eight accomplishments. The obstacle before accomplishment is threefold.

[tal-a08-v282] Above the worlds beginning with aṇimā there are three rows connected with teacher and disciple. Their threefold division is explained by the influence of the three qualities.

[tal-a08-v283] Above those rows is the eightfold set of nāḍī-knowledges beginning with iḍā. In the soul there is established a power made of sound, called expansion.

[tal-a08-v284] A soul that is not an agent cannot truly be established as the doer. Even if the soul is not an agent, it may still stand as an assisting cause.

[tal-a08-v285] Otherwise one would have to treat the soul as part of the effect, which would undermine the doctrine that the effect pre-exists. Therefore, in such a case, there is a specific power belonging to the soul.

[tal-a08-v286] Taking on that many forms, that power attains fullness. Above the eight nāḍīs, an eightfold set of forms is taught.

[tal-a08-v287] At the level of the puruṣa principle there is an eightfold embodied set: effect, cause, suffering, pleasure, knowledge, what is to be accomplished, the instruments, and the means.

[tal-a08-v288] Beyond the eightfold forms is the world of the ten bodily observances: non-harm, truth, non-stealing, continence, freedom from deceit, freedom from anger, and duties toward the teacher.

[tal-a08-v289] In the principle of the person are the ten declared qualities, including service, purity, contentment, and straightness. There too is situated a sixteenfold set ending with smell.

[tal-a08-v290] Starting from the world called the body-bond, the qualities of intellect appear. There the ego is present in eightfold and threefold forms, along with bonds beginning with desire.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ūhaḥ śabdo@dhyayanaṃ duḥkhavighātāstrayaḥ suhṛtprāptiḥ / dānaṃ ca siddhayo@ṣṭau siddheḥ pūrvo@ṅkuśastrividhaḥ aṇimādyūrdhvatastisraḥ paṅktayo guruśiṣyagāḥ / tatrāpi triguṇacchāyāyogāt tritvamudāhṛtam nāḍīvidyāṣṭakaṃ cordhvaṃ paṅktīnāṃ syādiḍādikam / puṃsi nādamayī śaktiḥ prasarākhyā ca yatsthitā na hyakartā pumānkartuḥ kāraṇatvaṃ ca saṃsthitam / akartaryapi vā puṃsi sahakāritayā sthite śeṣakāryātmataiṣṭavyānyathā satkāryahānitaḥ / tasmāttathāvidhe kārye yā śaktiḥ puruṣasya sā tāvanti rūpāṇyādāya pūrṇatāmadhigacchati / nāḍyaṣṭakordhve kathitaṃ vigrahāṣṭakamucyate kāryaṃ heturduḥkhaṃ sukhaṃ ca vijñānasādhyakaraṇāni / sādhanamiti vigrahatāyugaṣṭakaṃ bhavati puṃstattve bhuvanaṃ dehadharmāṇāṃ daśānāṃ vigrahāṣṭakāt / ahiṃsā satyamasteyaṃ brahmākalkākrudho guroḥ śuśrūṣāśaucasantoṣā ṛjuteti daśoditāḥ / puṃstattva eva gandhāntaṃ sthitaṃ ṣoḍaśakaṃ punaḥ ārabhya dehapāśākhyaṃ puraṃ buddhiguṇāstataḥ / tatraivāṣṭāvahaṃkārastridhā kāmādikāstathā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v291] The bonds are threefold: adventitious, of the Ganeshas, and of the Vidyeshvaras. They are present in the person and block the path to liberation.

[tal-a08-v292] Whatever is other than the supreme Shiva, whose nature is nondual consciousness, freedom, and beauty, is called a bond.

[tal-a08-v293] Thus, even though the supreme Lord remains full, when personhood is assumed there arises a wondrous non-recognition of his own nature; from that come persons.

[tal-a08-v294] All the bonds, whether stated or unstated and described in the Paratantra, are present in the person. By purifying them there, one is freed from worldly becoming.

[tal-a08-v295] Above the person, in niyati, dwell ten Shankaras, golden and very white. In the principle of time dwell ten Shivas.

[tal-a08-v296] In raga is the world of Viresha, a city of teachers and students, with ten million and sixteen thousand attendants for each.

[tal-a08-v297] In impure knowledge there is a world shining with nine Shaktis, beginning with Vama and extending up to Manonmani.

[tal-a08-v298] In kala is the supreme world of the three great gods. Beyond that is maya, a threefold domain filled chiefly with countless millions.

[tal-a08-v299] That maya is pervaded by cavities called bhaga, as taught in the Shaiva scripture. Again, there is a group of eight great gods extending to the measure of a thumb at night.

[tal-a08-v300] Likewise, in the teaching of Shrimalini, the powers beginning with Vama are described as ruling the eight circles; in the earlier sacred teaching they are said to begin from the level of the person.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-pāśā āgantukagāṇeśavaidyeśvarabheditāḥ / trividhāste sthitāḥ puṃsi mokṣamārgoparodhakāḥ yatkiṃcitparamādvaitasaṃvitsvātantryasundarāt / parācchivāduktarūpādanyattatpāśa ucyate tadevaṃ puṃstvamāpanne pūrṇe@pi parameśvare / tatsvarūpāparijñānaṃ citraṃ hi puruṣāstataḥ uktānuktāstu ye pāśāḥ paratantroktalakṣaṇāḥ / te puṃsi sarve tāṃstatra śodhayanmucyate bhavāt puṃsa ūrdhva tu niyatistatrasthāḥ śaṃkarā daśa / hemābhāḥ susitāḥ kālatattve tu daśa te śivāḥ koṭiḥ ṣoḍaśasāhasraṃ pratyekaṃ parivāriṇaḥ / rāge vīreśabhuvanaṃ gurvantevāsināṃ puram puraṃ cāśuddhavidyāyāṃ syācchaktinavakojjvalam / manonmanyantagāstāśca vāmādyāḥ parikīrtitāḥ kalāyāṃ syānmahādevatrayasya puramuttamam / tato māyā tripuṭikā mukhyato@nantakoṭibhiḥ ākrāntā sā bhagabilaiḥ proktaṃ śaivyāṃ tanau punaḥ / aṅguṣṭhamātraparyantaṃ mahādevāṣṭakaṃ niśi cakrāṣṭakādhipatyena tathā śrīmālinīmate / vāmādyāḥ puruṣādau ye proktāḥ śrīpūrvaśāsane

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v301] In the Shaiva scripture they are placed in the principle of maya, under Ananta: skull-vow observers, those who offer their own limbs, and practitioners of harsh austerities.

[tal-a08-v302] Fearless and observing the sword-edge vow, knowing the principles, they gradually ascend through each principle until they reach the place where the lord is called Ananta.

[tal-a08-v303] And it is said that beyond him is the abode of the lord of Ananta, the god who performs creation, maintenance, and dissolution, and who guards the door of the cave and the bhaga.

[tal-a08-v304] Drawing them out again and again from the cavity of maya, he bestows on persons merits, powers such as minuteness, knowledges, austerities, pleasures, and yogic attainments.

[tal-a08-v305] Empowered by his energy, all the lords from Ananta onward, down to those beginning with Shatabhava, shine like lamps dispelling darkness in the office of the cave.

[tal-a08-v306] Presiding over the unmanifest, Shiva brings forth the world by the command of Shambhu, because he is the cause of authority over both the pure and impure streams.

[tal-a08-v307] Those first established in that great station endowed with Shiva's qualities, beginning with Ananta, become the agents of the world's creation, maintenance, and dissolution.

[tal-a08-v308] This has been called the cavity of maya. Beyond it is the cave, the womb of the world, where generation occurs as the stirring of the lord's power takes effect.

[tal-a08-v309] In the womb-openings, rich with various desires and called bhaga, when the lord desires the goddess who follows his will, the generative process begins.

[tal-a08-v310] In each bhaga, offspring beginning with the unmanifest are born from her. They are so extremely subtle that their nature is not described in the prescribed texts.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-te māyātattva evoktāstanau śaivyāmanantataḥ / kapālavratinaḥ svāṅgahotāraḥ kaṣṭatāpasāḥ sarvābhayāḥ khaḍgadhārāvratāstattattvavedinaḥ / kramāttattattvamāyānti yatreśo@nanta ucyate uktaṃ ca tasya parataḥ sthānamanantādhipasya devasya / sthitivilayasargakarturguhābhagadvārapālasya dharmānaṇimādiguṇāñjñānāni tapaḥsukhāni yogāṃśca / māyābilātpradatte puṃsāṃ niṣkṛṣya niṣkṛṣya tacchaktīddhasvabalā guhādhikārāndhakāraguṇadīpāḥ / sarve@nantapramukhā dīpyante śatabhavapramukhāntāḥ so@vyaktamadhiṣṭhāya prakaroti jaganniyogataḥ śambhoḥ / śuddhāśuddhasroto@dhikārahetuḥ śivo yasmāt śivaguṇayoge tasmin mahati pade ye pratiṣṭhitāḥ prathamam / te@nantāderjagataḥ sargasthitivilayakartāraḥ māyābilamidamuktaṃ paratastu guhā jagadyoniḥ / utpattyā teṣvasyāḥ patiśaktikṣobhamanuvidhīyamāneṣu yonivivareṣu nānākāmasamṛddheṣu bhagasaṃjñā / kāmayate patirenāmicchānuvidhāyinīṃ yadā devīm pratibhagamavyaktādyāḥ prajāstadāsyāḥ prajāyante / teṣāmatisūkṣmāṇāmetāvattvaṃ na varṇyate vidhiṣu

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v311] Just as many enclosed inner rooms can exist within one hall, so many womb-cavities exist within the single head-hall of maya.

[tal-a08-v312] Covered by subtle layers and walls of maya, invisible to one another, countless happy Rudras dwell there in each cavity.

[tal-a08-v313] Dwellers in each world are taught by teachers as having attained union, proximity, or supreme same-world residence.

[tal-a08-v314] Even words of the accomplished, uttered long ago, are worn out; numbers of streams are not spoken again from endless rebirth.

[tal-a08-v315] Therefore, from one hell up to door guardians, other streams too are similarly arranged and to be known.

[tal-a08-v316] In unmanifest time, by cave, nature, and art, the own modification is woven across and through, pervaded, measured, full, and encircled.

[tal-a08-v317] In the middle, three sheaths of that contain rudras: six in the lower interval, one above, and five; these twelve are determined.

[tal-a08-v318] The deep difficult lords, hari, hara, dasha lords, and three-time lords; these six in the endless middle are auspicious brahman-lord, knowledge-lord, world-shiva.

[tal-a08-v319] Thus in those five and six sheaths, by turning of that, position revolves; indeed the endless god is in every way in the middle.

[tal-a08-v320] By the pair of six upper and lower skull sheaths, by turning of that, pervaded in the middle by eight directional ones, the knot stated in Matanga scripture.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-avavarakāṇyekasminyadvatsāle bahūni baddhāni / yonibilānyekasmiṃstadvanmāyāśiraḥsāle māyāpaṭalaiḥ sūkṣmaiḥ kuḍyaiḥ pihitāḥ parasparamadṛśyāḥ / nivasanti tatra rudrāḥ sukhinaḥ pratibilamasaṃkhyātāḥ sthāne sāyujyagatāḥ sāmīpyagatāḥ pare salokasthāḥ / pratibhuvanamevamayaṃ nivāsināṃ gurubhiruddiṣṭaḥ api sarvasiddhavācaḥ kṣīyerandīrghakālamudgīrṇāḥ / na punaryonyānantyāducyante srotasāṃ saṃkhyāḥ tasmānnirayādyekaṃ yatproktaṃ dvārapālaparyantam / srotastenānyānyapi tulyavidhānāni vedyāni avyaktakale guhayā prakṛtikalābhyāṃ vikāra ātmīyaḥ / otaḥ proto vyāptaḥ kalitaḥ pūrṇaḥ parikṣiptaḥ madhye puṭatrayaṃ tasyā rudrāḥ ṣaḍadhare@ntare / eka ūrdhve ca pañceti dvādaśaite nirūpitāḥ gahanāsādhyau hariharadaśeśvarau trikalagopatī ṣaḍime / madhye@nantaḥ kṣemo dvijeśavidyeśaviśvaśivāḥ iti pañca teṣu pañcasu ṣaṭsu ca puṭageṣu tatparāvṛttyā / parivarttate sthitiḥ kila devo@nantastu sarvathā madhye ūrdhvādharagakapālakapuṭaṣaṭkayugena tatparāvṛttyā / madhyato@ṣṭābhirdiksthairvyāpto granthirmataṅgaśāstroktaḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v321] In the Sri Sara teaching, again this is declared as six sheaths; this knot-principle is the work of maya, then maya.

[tal-a08-v322] The maya principle is indeed pervasive, deep, formless, place of all dissolution; there world-division is not fit, that knot therefore.

[tal-a08-v323] The endless lord of maya principle simultaneously agitates collected atoms; she produces night by endless own enclosures.

[tal-a08-v324] By that, the declared veil net from kala to earth end is countless and various; maya alone is one and to be distinguished.

[tal-a08-v325] It is said in the Sri prior scripture: the earth-manifest pair is countless, called night-power, but one-natured.

[tal-a08-v326] Bonds previously said, om-syllables, five-eight, sage's family and womb, speech-goddess; one born in her is not born again.

[tal-a08-v327] At initiation time, in earth-path purification, all that goes the earth path of the endless is fully established near him.

[tal-a08-v328] Accomplishable, giver, subduer, meditator, ash: five dots, with formation, marked by five-meaning secret rudra goad heart.

[tal-a08-v329] Attraction and mirror, this eight of measures; all with unlost powers are authorities of maya principle.

[tal-a08-v330] Those with maya bodies enjoy their own enjoyment; at the end of dissolution, indeed by the endless, they are withdrawn, but at day's beginning.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-śrīsāraśāsane punareṣā ṣaṭpuṭatayā vinirdiṣṭā / granthyākhyamidaṃ tattvaṃ māyākāryaṃ tato māyā māyātattvaṃ vibhu kila gahanamarūpaṃ samastavilayapadam / tatra na bhuvanavibhāgo yukto granthāvasau tasmāt māyātattvādhipatiḥ so@nantaḥ samuditānvicāryāṇūn / yugapatkṣobhayati niśāṃ sā sūte saṃpuṭairanantaiḥ svaiḥ tena kalādidharāntaṃ yaduktamāvaraṇajālamakhilaṃ tat / niḥsaṃkhyaṃ ca vicitraṃ māyaivaikā tvabhinneyam uktaṃ śrīpūrvaśāstre ca dharāvyaktātmakaṃ dvayam / asaṃkhyātaṃ niśāśaktisaṃjñaṃ tvekasvarūpakam pāśāḥ puroktāḥ praṇavāḥ pañcamānāṣṭakaṃ muneḥ / kulaṃ yoniśca vāgīśī yasyāṃ jāto na jāyate dīkṣākāle@dharādhvasthaśuddhau yaccādharādhvagam / anantasya samīpe tu tatsarvaṃ pariniṣṭhitam sādhyo dātā damano dhyāno bhasmeti bindavaḥ pañca / pañcārthaguhyarudrāṅkuśahṛdayalakṣaṇaṃ ca savyūham ākarṣādarśau cetyaṣṭakametatpramāṇānām / aluptavibhavāḥ sarve māyātattvādhikāriṇaḥ māyāmayaśarīrāste bhogaṃ svaṃ paribhuñjate / pralayānte hyanantena saṃhṛtāste tvaharmukhe

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v331] By the grace of another endless, even wise ones think the supreme asleep-awakened, dull with self-will opinion.

[tal-a08-v332] Those situated in the maya interval know only their own self as cause; therefore maya goddess stands supreme, deluding creatures.

[tal-a08-v333] She is the power of the god of gods, doing very difficult things, obstructing without enmity; by her minds are made to wander.

[tal-a08-v334] Disputants here dispute this principle, this not-this; those not devoted to guru, deva, agni scriptures are lowest men.

[tal-a08-v335] Abandoning the true path, it certainly leads them to the false path, those clinging to dry logic.

[tal-a08-v336] Maya indeed deludes them in non-liberation, with desire for liberation; thus cut by the sword of shiva initiation and the sword of shiva knowledge.

[tal-a08-v337] No other cause sprouts again; cutting is directed toward it, and pure great knowledge stands above great maya.

[tal-a08-v338] Vageshvari stands there in the city of nine, including Vama, Jyeshtha, Raudri, Kali, Kalavikarani, Balavikarika, and others.

[tal-a08-v339] Mathani, Damani, Manonmani, and all those yellow powers amount to seven crores of chief mantra powers established in the knowledge principle.

[tal-a08-v340] Here there are lotus-shaped cities, seven knowledge queens beginning with triguna, and seven arbuda lords.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-anyānantaprasādena vibudhā api taṃ param / suptabuddhaṃ manyamānāḥ svatantrammanyatājaḍāḥ svātmānameva jānanti hetuṃ māyāntarālagāḥ / ataḥ paraṃ sthitā māyā devī jantuvimohinī devadevasya sā śaktiratidurghaṭakāritā / nirvairaparipanthinyā tayā bhramitabuddhayaḥ idaṃ tattvamidaṃ neti vivadantīha vādinaḥ / gurudevāgniśāstreṣu ye na bhaktā narādhamāḥ satpathaṃ tānparityājya sotpathaṃ nayati dhruvam / asadyuktivicārajñāñchuṣkatarkāvalambinaḥ bhramayatyeva tānmāyā hyamokṣe mokṣalipsayā / śivadīkṣāsinā cchinnā śivajñānāsinā tathā na prarohetpunarnānyo hetustacchedanaṃ prati / mahāmāyordhvataḥ śuddhā mahāvidyātha mātṛkā vāgīśvarī ca tatrasthaṃ vāmādinavasatpuram / vāmā jyeṣṭhā raudrī kālī kalavikaraṇībalavikārike tathā mathanī damanī manonmanī ca tridṛśaḥ pītāḥ samastāstāḥ / saptakoṭyo mukhyamantrā vidyātattve@tra saṃsthitāḥ ekaikārbudalakṣāṃśāḥ padmākārapurā iha / vidyārājñyastriguṇyādyāḥ sapta saptārbudeśvarāḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v341] Above the knowledge principle is the aisha principle, ascending in order from Shikhanda to Ananta, joined with eight cities.

[tal-a08-v342] Shikhanda, Shrigala, Murti, one-eye, one-rudra, highest Shiva, subtle Rudra, Ananta, and the eight Vidyeshvaras are named.

[tal-a08-v343] In the ascending upward placement of the seven, Ananta is the leader and lord, to be meditated and worshipped increasingly.

[tal-a08-v344] Three crores are established with the chief mantra lords; these leaders are thereby Vidyeshas and world rulers.

[tal-a08-v345] The gurus said this in the Shiva-body teachings: a god with eight shakti pairs sits on the guha throne.

[tal-a08-v346] From the deep beginning to the end of hell, he creates, assigns Rudras, and uplifts men through Manonmani, remaining middle-standing.

[tal-a08-v347] Those uplifted by him enter supreme principle contemplation; he is again appointed by Shiva among path dwellers and atoms.

[tal-a08-v348] After the completed lord assignment, Ananta lord enters that abode with many soul mantra crores, while subtle Rudra extinguishes.

[tal-a08-v349] The lord establishes the first atom in Shikhanda's place; thus eight proceed in order until the abodes, by the single guru.

[tal-a08-v350] Those eight, seated on lotus thrones with eight shakti yoga, make liberation for countless beings.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-vidyātattvordhvamaiśaṃ tu tattvaṃ tatra kramordhvagam / śikhaṇḍyādyamanantāntaṃ purāṣṭakayutaṃ puram śikhaṇḍī śrīgalo mūrtirekanetraikarudrakau / śivottamaḥ sūkṣmarudro@nanto vidyeśvarāṣṭakam kramādūrdhvordhvasaṃsthānaṃ saptānāṃ nāyako vibhuḥ / ananta eva dhyeyaśca pūjyaścāpyuttarottaraḥ mukhyamantreśvarāṇāṃ yat sārdhaṃ koṭitrayaṃ sthitam / tannāyakā ime tena vidyeśāścakravartinaḥ uktaṃ ca gurubhiritthaṃ śivatanvādyeṣu śāsaneṣvetat / bhagabilaśatakalitaguhāmūrdhāsanago@ṣṭaśaktiyugdevaḥ gahanādyaṃ nirayāntaṃ sṛjati ca rudrāṃśca viniyuṅkte / uddharati manonmanyā puṃsasteṣveva bhavati madhyasthaḥ te tenodastacitaḥ paratattvālocane@bhiniviśante / sa punaradhaḥ pathavartiṣvadhikṛta evāṇuṣu śivena avasitapativiniyogaḥ sārdhamanekātmamantrakoṭībhiḥ / nirvātyanantanāthastaddhāmāviśati sūkṣmarudrastu anugṛhyāṇumapūrvaṃ sthāpayati patiḥ śikhaṇḍinaḥ sthāne / ityaṣṭau paripāṭyā yāvaddhāmāni yāti gururekaḥ tāvadasaṃkhyātānāṃ jantūnāṃ nirvṛtiṃ kurute / te@ṣṭāvapi śaktyaṣṭakayogāmalajalaruhāsanāsīnāḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v351] They behold the god dwelling in the heart, the supreme cause Ananta, meditating on the peaceful cause in their own heart.

[tal-a08-v352] Seven crores of pure mantras meditate, extending from Maya to sun ray; becoming is called non-becoming beginning with Ananta.

[tal-a08-v353] This end of Shiva pure quality authority is also rejected here, because the appointability of the seen and granted is Shaiva.

[tal-a08-v354] Desired cessation is non-becoming below, but it does not become so, because it departs from the lord; causality and effecthood come from the accomplished.

[tal-a08-v355] In Shiva accomplishment like armor, the extreme and middle-standing pair is named, and the city of four—dharma, knowledge, dispassion, and mastery—is identified.

[tal-a08-v356] In this Ishvara principle, the form covering is known; Vama, Jyeshtha, and Raudri adorn the three worlds.

[tal-a08-v357] The subtle covering in the Isha principle, named by the best gurus, runs from Aisha to Sadashiva and is adorned with the knowledge-action pair.

[tal-a08-v358] The pure covering is thus said; from it comes the supreme, and then the knowledge covering shines with two powers of being and non-being.

[tal-a08-v359] The power covering, called measure, is determined in scripture; it is adorned by Tejasvi and Dhruvesha.

[tal-a08-v360] The Tejasvi covering is followed by the measure covering, which is adorned with three pure covering cities.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-ālokayanti devaṃ hṛdayasthaṃ kāraṇaṃ paramam / taṃ bhagavantamanantaṃ dhyāyantaḥ svahṛdi kāraṇaṃ śāntam saptānudhyāyantyapi mantrāṇāṃ koṭayaḥ śuddhāḥ / māyādiravīcyanto bhavastvanantādirucyate@pyabhavaḥ śivaśuddhaguṇādhīkārāntaḥ so@pyeṣa heyaśca / atrāpi yato dṛṣṭānugrāhyāṇāṃ niyojyatā śaivī iṣṭā ca tannivṛttirhyabhavastvadhare na bhūyate yasmāt / patyurapasarpati yataḥ kāraṇatā kāryatā ca siddhebhyaḥ kañcukavacchivasiddhau tāvatibhavasaṃjñayātimadhyasthau / dharmajñānavirāgaiśyacatuṣṭayapuraṃ tu yat rūpāvaraṇasaṃjñaṃ tattattve@sminnaiśvare viduḥ / vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca raudrīti bhuvanatrayaśobhitam sūkṣmāvaraṇamākhyātamīśatattve gurūttamaiḥ / aiśātsādāśivaṃ jñānakriyāyugalamaṇḍitam śuddhāvaraṇamityāhuruktā śuddhāvṛteḥ param / vidyāvṛtistato bhāvābhāvaśaktidvayojjvalā śaktyāvṛtiḥ pramāṇākhyā tataḥ śāstre nirūpitā / śaktyāvṛtestu tejasvidhruveśābhyāmalaṅkṛtam tejasvyāvaraṇaṃ vedapurā mānāvṛtistataḥ / mānāvṛteḥ suśuddhāvṛtpuratritayaśobhitā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v361] Above the very-pure covering there is a single Shaiva city. Above the Shiva-covering, they say, lies the covering called the liberation-covering.

[tal-a08-v362] In this liberation-covering, eleven Rudras are described. Above the liberation-covering there is a single-city covering called the fixed one.

[tal-a08-v363] Above the fixed covering is the will-covering. There dwell those Shivas inside the house of the Lord's will, and that city is said to be one.

[tal-a08-v364] Above the will-covering is the one called the awakened covering, frequented by the eight directional Rudras. Above the awakened covering lies the great covenant-covering.
