[tal-a08-v365] The covenant-covering encloses the covering of Ananta within five worlds. Above it lies the auspicious-Shiva realm, and there is the great world called Sadakhya.

[tal-a08-v366] In that world dwells the god Sadashiva. His powers of knowledge and action are on his left and right, while his supreme will rests in his lap.

[tal-a08-v367] By that will, Sadashiva performs the five acts beginning with creation. With him are the five Brahmas, the six limbs, the group of eight beginning with Sakala, and other Shivas.

[tal-a08-v368] The auspicious Shiva is surrounded by those ten and eighteen Rudras. The five Brahmas are Sadyojata, Vama, Aghora, Purusha, and Ishana, and the heart is named among them.

[tal-a08-v369] They declare the six limbs to be head, tuft, armor, eye, and weapon, together with the heart. Along with them are Sakala, Akala, Shunya, Kaladhya, Kha, and Kshapana as the last.

[tal-a08-v370] The throat-and-lip one is the eighth, and this group of eight Saktalas is traditionally transmitted. Then are named Omkara, Shiva, Dipta, Hetu, Isha, Dasheshaka, Sushiva, and Kala.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-suśuddhāvaraṇādūrdhva śaivamekapuraṃ bhavet / śivāvṛterūrdhvamāhurmokṣāvaraṇasaṃjñitam asyāṃ mokṣāvṛtau rudrā ekādaśa nirūpitāḥ / mokṣāvaraṇatastvekapuramāvaraṇaṃ dhruvam ūrdhve dhruvāvṛtericchāvaraṇaṃ tatra te śivāḥ / īśvarecchāgṛhāntasthāstatpuraṃ caikamucyate icchāvṛteḥ prabuddhākhyaṃ digrudrāṣṭakacarcitam / prabuddhāvaraṇādūrdhva samayāvaraṇaṃ mahat bhuvanaiḥ pañcabhirgarbhīkṛtānantasamāvṛti / sāmayātsauśivaṃ tatra sādākhyaṃ bhuvanaṃ mahat tasminsadāśivo devastasya savyāpasavyayoḥ / jñānakriye parecchā tu śaktirutsaṅgagāminī sṛṣṭyādipañcakṛtyāni kurute sa tayecchayā / pañca brahmāṇyaṅgaṣaṭkaṃ sakalādyaṣṭakaṃ śivāḥ daśāṣṭādaśa rudrāśca taireva suśivo vṛtaḥ / sadyo vāmāghorau puruṣeśau brahmapañcakaṃ hṛdayam mūrdhaśikhāvarmadṛgastramaṅgāni ṣaṭ prāhuḥ / sakalākalaśūnyaiḥ saha kalāḍhyakhamalaṅkṛte kṣapaṇamantyam kaṇṭhyauṣṭhyamaṣṭamaṃ kila sakalāṣṭakametadāmnātam / oṃ kāraśivau dīpto hetvīśadaśeśakau suśivakālau

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v371] Sukshma, Sutejas, and Sharva are these ten Shivas. Then, beginning from the east, come Vijaya, Nihshvasa, Svayambhuva, Vahni, Vira, and Raurava.

[tal-a08-v372] Mukuta, Visara, Indu, Bindu, Prodgita, Lalita, Siddha, Rudra, Santana, Shiva, Para, Kirana, and Paramesha are remembered as the Rudras.

[tal-a08-v373] All these Rudras have knowledges that bear names equal to their own. They are surrounded by crores of mantra-sages and joined with Vibhu, Vama, and the Rudras together with their powers.

[tal-a08-v374] Sushiva's seat is a very white lotus with countless petals, endowed with Tara and other powers. The group of powers and Rudras is present both in his retinue and on his seat.

[tal-a08-v375] In each one's own retinue there are countless crores beyond measure. They are freed from the impurity of maya, yet remain established only in their office.

[tal-a08-v376] In the covering of Sushiva, the Rudras are all-knowing and full of all powers. When the bondage of their office dissolves, they become peaceful, take on the form of Shiva, and are no longer subject to rebirth.

[tal-a08-v377] Above is the radiant covering of bindu. There is a moon-bright lotus, and there Shiva as Shantyatita is adorned, resting in the lap of his power.

[tal-a08-v378] He is surrounded by the retinue of the kala group beginning with Nivritti, and by crores of cities of countless Rudras and their powers.

[tal-a08-v379] In the revered Matanga scripture, the highest principle called Laya is, by that technical name, identified here with bindu.

[tal-a08-v380] That bright principle, made of four forms and both with parts and without parts, is where enjoyment is said to take place. This is how it is described here.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-sūkṣmasutejaḥśarvāḥ śivāḥ daśaite@tra pūrvādeḥ / vijayo niḥśvāsaśca svāyambhuvo vahnivīrarauravakāḥ mukuṭavisarenduvinduprodgītā lalitasiddharudrau ca / santānaśivau parakiraṇapārameśā iti smṛtā rudrāḥ sarveṣāmeteṣāṃ jñānāni viduḥ svatulyanāmāni / mantramunikoṭiparivṛta matha vibhuvāmādirudratacchaktiyutam tārādiśaktijuṣṭaṃ suśivāsanamatisitakajamasaṃkhyadalam / yaḥ śaktirudravargaḥ parivāre viṣṭare ca suśivasya pratyekamasya nijanijaparivāre parārdhakoṭayo@saṃkhyāḥ / māyāmalanirmuktāḥ kevalamadhikāramātrasaṃrūḍhāḥ suśivāvaraṇe rudrāḥ sarvajñāḥ sarvaśaktisampūrṇāḥ / adhikārabandhavilaye śāntāḥ śivarūpiṇo punarbhavinaḥ ūrdhve bindvāvṛtirdīptā tatra tatra padmaṃ śaśiprabham / śāntyatītaḥ śivastatra tacchaktyutsaṅgabhūṣitaḥ nivṛttyādikalāvargaparivārasamāvṛtaḥ / asaṃkhyarudratacchaktipurakoṭibhirāvṛtaḥ śrīmanmataṅgaśāstre ca layākhyaṃ tattvamuttamam / pāribhāṣikamityetannāmnā bindurihocyate caturmūrtimayaṃ śubhraṃ yattatsakalaniṣkalam / tasminbhogaḥ samuddiṣṭa ityatredaṃ ca varṇitam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v381] Because Nivritti and the other kalas are extremely subtle, embodiment beginning from earth does not take shape in the usual way. Since the Mother is absorbed in flashing great knowledge, it is not distinctly perceived.

[tal-a08-v382] Just as earth particles in gold do not appear separately because its fiery nature predominates, so too the elements in the bodies of the higher and lower Rudras do not appear separately.

[tal-a08-v383] Above bindu is the half-moon. From that come kala, moonlight, radiance, splendor, and the pure one. These five are the obstructing powers.

[tal-a08-v384] The best of teachers declare that in Nirodhini there are five kalas: Rundhani, Rodhani, Roddhri, Jnanabodha, and Tamopaha.

[tal-a08-v385] The half-measure is called bindu, which has the form of space and four phases. Half of that is the half-moon, and by an eighth part of that comes nirodhikā.

[tal-a08-v386] Rodhikā blocks the causal lords beginning with Brahma; one should abandon it. Then, after piercing this nirodhikā, one reaches the supreme world called Sadakhya.

[tal-a08-v387] There, in supreme form, abides the one whose great body is made of the five mantras. Thus, above the covering of bindu that ends in the half-moon and nirodhi, there is a great presence.

[tal-a08-v388] Nāda is like the filaments of a flower and is surrounded by great beings. There are four worlds in the directions and a fifth in the center.

[tal-a08-v389] Indhikā, Dīpikā, Rodhikā, and the upward-going Mocikā are there. In the middle is a lotus, and there the upward-moving one is surrounded by its powers.

[tal-a08-v390] Above nāda is the suṣumna realm. There the lord who bears its powers is surrounded on the left and right by Piṅgalā and Iḍā.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-nivṛttyādeḥ susūkṣmatvāddharādyārabdhadehatā / mātuḥ sphūrjanmahājñānalīnatvānna vibhāvyate udrikta taijasatvena hemno bhūparamāṇavaḥ / yathā pṛthaṅna bhāntyevamūrdhvādhorudradehagāḥ bindūrdhve@rdhenduretasya kalā jyotsnā ca tadvatī / kāntiḥ prabhā ca vimalā pañcaitā rodhikāstataḥ rundhanī rodhanī roddhrī jñānabodhā tamopahā / etāḥ pañca kalāḥ prāhurnirodhinyāṃ gurūttamāh ardhamātraḥ smṛto bindurvyomarūpī catuṣkalaḥ / tadardhamardhacandrastadaṣṭāṃśena nirodhikā hetūnbrahmādikān runddhe rodhikāṃ tāṃ tyajettataḥ / nirodhikāmimāṃ bhittvā sādākhyaṃ bhuvanaṃ param pararūpeṇa yatrāste pañcamantramahātanuḥ / ityardhendunirodhyantabindvāvṛtyūrdhvato mahān nādaḥ kiñjalkasadṛśo mahadbhiḥ puruṣairvṛtaḥ / catvāri bhuvanānyatra dikṣu madhye ca pañcamam indhikā dīpikā caiva rodhikā mocikordhvagā / madhye@tra padmaṃ tatrordhvagāmī tacchaktibhirvṛtaḥ nādordhvatastu sauṣumnaṃ tatra tacchaktibhṛtprabhuḥ / tadīśaḥ piṅgalelābhyāṃ vṛtaḥ savyāpasavyayoḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v391] The goddess Suṣumnā, resting in the lord's lap and shining like the moon, strings together the whole path, both above and below.

[tal-a08-v392] The support of nāda and suṣumnā pierces this entire universe; it goes out below by the downward power and above from the crown by the upward power.

[tal-a08-v393] Absorbed through the channel in the cavity of Brahma, that unmanifest, resonant, imperishable sound resounds in all beings, empowered by Śiva's śakti.

[tal-a08-v394] Above Suṣumnā is the covering called the brahma cavity. There dwells Brahmā, white, three-eyed, bearing a trident, five-faced, and crowned with the moon.

[tal-a08-v395] In his lap sits the supreme goddess Brahmāṇī, who moves on the path of liberation and both obstructs and grants release. Piercing through her, one comes to the upward Kuṇḍalinī.

[tal-a08-v396] That śakti is like a sleeping serpent and is called the support of the universe. Within her are the subtle, the very subtle, Amṛtā, Amitā, and other powers.

[tal-a08-v397] In the middle is Vyāpinī, and within her is Vyāpīśa, the bearer of Vyāpinī. This is the śakti principle, whose manifestation extends all the way down to earth.

[tal-a08-v398] Then comes the Śiva principle. Established in the four directions are Vyāpī, the sky-natured lord Ananta, and those who share in his powers.

[tal-a08-v399] In the middle there is the unsupported one: the god of gods, Anāśrita, bearing his śakti in his lap and shining with the radiance of a hundred crore suns.

[tal-a08-v400] Above the Śiva principle is the supreme śakti called Samanā. She abides as the active agent of all causes.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-yā prabhoraṅkagā devī suṣumnā śaśisaprabhā / grathito@dhvā tayā sarva ūrdhvaścādhastanastathā nādaḥsuṣumnādhārastu bhittvā viśvamidaṃ jagat / adhaḥśaktyā vinirgacchedūrdhvaśaktyā ca mūrdhataḥ nāḍyā brahmabile līnaḥ so@vyaktadhvanirakṣaraḥ / nadansarveṣu bhūteṣu śivaśaktyā hyadhiṣṭhitaḥ suṣumnordhve brahmabilasaṃjñayāvaraṇaṃ tridṛk / tatra brahmā sitaḥ śūlī pañcāsyaḥ śaśiśekharaḥ tasyotsaṅge parā devī brahmāṇī mokṣamārgagā / roddhrī dātrī ca mokṣasya tāṃ bhittvā cordhvakuṇḍalī śaktiḥ suptāhisadṛśī sā viśvādhāra ucyate / tasyāṃ sūkṣmā susūkṣmā ca tathānye amṛtāmite madhyato vyāpinī tasyāṃ vyāpīśo vyāpinīdharaḥ / śaktitattvamidaṃ yasya prapañco@yaṃ dharāntakaḥ śivatattvaṃ tatastatra caturdikkaṃ vyavasthitāḥ / vyāpī vyomātmako@nanto@nāthastacchaktibhāginaḥ madhye tvanāśritaṃ tatra devadevo hyanāśritaḥ / tacchaktyutsaṅgabhṛtsūryaśatakoṭisamaprabhaḥ śivatattvordhvataḥ śaktiḥ parā sā samanāhvayā / sarveṣāṃ kāraṇānāṃ sā kartṛbhūtā vyavasthitā

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v401] Empowered by Śiva, she bears many cosmic eggs. Resting upon her, Lord Śiva performs the five acts.

[tal-a08-v402] Samanā is the instrument of that great causal lord. The unsupported principle, in activity, is the occasioning cause and is called the cause.

[tal-a08-v403] Through her the all-pervading lord presides over the five causes. This unsupported, lordly, endless, sky-bodied one does so always.

[tal-a08-v404] He impels the pervading lord by his own śakti as instrument. Below that abides Māyā in the form of karma, and below that is the śakti Kuṇḍalinī.

[tal-a08-v405] The arising of the world as effect begins with nāda, bindu, and so on. In the teaching, this includes everything from the earthly level up to Sadāśiva.

[tal-a08-v406] All that is declared to be produced and subject to arising and destruction. Now I will present the measure of all the worlds as it was taught to me by my own gurus.

[tal-a08-v407] That will now be explained briefly so that the mind may quickly move through it. Within the cosmic egg are Ananta, Kāla, Kūṣmāṇḍa and Hāṭaka, and Brahmā and Hari.

[tal-a08-v408] There are one hundred Rudras with their hosts. Outside is Nivṛtti, which has one hundred and eight worlds, distributed individually across the sevenfold group of water, fire, wind, space, ego, intellect, and root.

[tal-a08-v409] The kalā level is declared to have fifty-six worlds, and so it is called pratiṣṭhā. Some, however, say that eight of its own lords are to be purified there.

[tal-a08-v410] Others say that all the worlds are to be purified. The teachers led by Śrī Bhūtirāja Miśra, however, say that a hundred Rudras are outside.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-bibhartyaṇḍānyanekāni śivena samadhiṣṭhitā / tadārūḍhaḥ śivaḥ kṛtyapañcakaṃ kurute prabhuḥ samanā karaṇaṃ tasya hetukarturmahośituḥ / anāśritaṃ tu vyāpāre nimittaṃ heturucyate tayādhitiṣṭhati vibhuḥ kāraṇānāṃ tu pañcakam / anāśrito@nāthamayamanantaṃ khavapuḥ sadā sa vyāpinaṃ prerayati svaśaktyā karaṇena tu / karmarūpā sthitā māyā yadadhaḥ śaktikuṇḍalī nādabindvādikaṃ kāryamityādijagadudbhavaḥ / yatsadāśivaparyantaṃ pārthivādyaṃ ca śāsane tatsarva prākṛtaṃ proktaṃ vināśotpattisaṃyutam / atha sakalabhuvanamānaṃ yanmahyaṃ nigaditaṃ nijairgurubhiḥ tadvakṣyate samāsādbuddhau yenāśu saṅkrāmet / aṇḍasyāntaranantaḥ kālaḥ kūṣmāṇḍahāṭakau brahmaharī rudrāḥ śataṃ savīraṃ bahirnivṛttistu sāṣṭaśatabhuvanā syāt / jalatejaḥsamīranabho@haṃkṛddhīmūlasaptake pratyekam aṣṭau ṣaṭpañcāśadbhuvanā tena pratiṣṭheti kalā kathitā / atra prāhuḥ śodhyānaṣṭau kecinnijāṣṭakādhipatīn anye tu samastānāṃ śodhyatvaṃ varṇayanti bhuvanānām / śrībhūtirājamiśrā guravaḥ prāhuḥ punarbahī rudraśatam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v411] This nivṛtti consists of eight Rudras within, together with Śarva. The Rudras named here are Kālī, Vīra, Dharā, Abdhi, Lakṣmī, Sarasvatī, and Guhya.

[tal-a08-v412] Thus the group of eight is in water. In fire there is a pair beyond Guhya; in wind there is the world of Vāyu. In space there are the group beginning with Gaya, Vyoma, the eight Pavitras, and a pair of worlds.

[tal-a08-v413] In ego there is the group of eight beginning with Chagala. Then, within the domain of space and ego-maker, there is the group of eight worlds of the tanmātras, sun, moon, and śruti, belonging to the gods of intellect and action.

[tal-a08-v414] There are ten worlds in the tanmātra group, and others in the sense group and in mind and ego; altogether there are twenty-two worlds.

[tal-a08-v415] In the intellect there are eight divine ones, a triad called Kṛt, Tejas, and Yoga, then Umā and her lord, then the eight Mūrtis, the twelve Suśivas, and Vīrabhadra.

[tal-a08-v416] Then come the eight Mahādevas; in the intellect the count is seventeen. In the guṇa tattva there are three sets of five, and altogether they know fifty-six worlds.

[tal-a08-v417] Although the eight Krodheśvaras are in mūla, the state of balanced guṇas, they are not counted again in pratiṣṭhā because they are treated as purified in the intellect.

[tal-a08-v418] Thus, in pratiṣṭhā, from the water tattva up to mūla, there are twenty-four tattvas, along with the satisfactions beginning with Ambā, those beginning with Tārā, and the siddhis beginning with Aṇimā.

[tal-a08-v419] There are teachers, teachers with disciples, groups of seers, and those beginning with Iḍā, together with the eight bodies. There is also the world of modifications beginning with smell, the eight qualities of intellect, ego-activity, and the qualities of the sense objects.

[tal-a08-v420] There is also the incidental group of twenty-seven beginning with Kāma, and likewise the groups of Gaṇeśas and Vidyeśas. Thus, among the bonds there are three worlds, and here in the puruṣa there are sixteen worlds.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-aṣṭāvantaḥ sākaṃ śarveṇetīdṛśī nivṛttiriyaṃ syāt / rudrāḥ kālī vīro dharābdhilakṣmyaḥ sarasvatī guhyam ityaṣṭakaṃ jale@nau vahnyatiguhyadvayaṃ maruti vāyoḥ / svapuraṃ gayādi khe ca vyoma pavitrāṣṭakaṃ ca bhuvanayugam abhimāne@haṅkāracchagalādyaṣṭakamathāntarā nabho@haṃkṛt / tanmātrārkenduśratipurāṣṭakaṃ buddhikarmadevānām daśa tanmātrasamūhe bhuvanaṃ punarakṣavargavinipatite / manasaścetyabhimāne dvāviṃśatireva bhuvanānām dhiyi daivīnāmaṣṭau kruttejoyogasaṃjñakaṃ trayaṃ tadumā / tatpatiratha mūrtyaṣṭakasuśivadvādaśakavīrabhadrāḥ syuḥ tadatha mahādevāṣṭakamiti buddhau saptadaśa saṃkhyā / guṇatattve paṅktitrayamiti ṣaṭpañcāśataṃ purāṇi viduḥ yadyapi guṇasāmyātmani mūle krodheśvarāṣṭakaṃ tathāpi dhiyi / tacchodhitamiti gaṇanāṃ na punaḥ prāptaṃ pratiṣṭhāyām iti jalatattvānmūlaṃ tattvacaturviṃśatiḥ pratiṣṭhāyām / ambādituṣṭivargastārādyāḥ siddhayo@ṇimādigaṇaḥ guravo guruśiṣyā ṛṣivarga iḍādiśca vigrahāṣṭakayuk / gandhādivikārapuraṃ buddhiguṇāṣṭakamahaṃkriyā viṣayaguṇāḥ kāmādisaptaviṃśakamāgantu tathā gaṇeśavidyeśamayau / iti pāśeṣu puratrayamitthaṃ puruṣe@tra bhuvanaṣoḍaśakam

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v421] In the tattva of restriction there are ten Śaṅkara worlds; in time there are ten Śiva worlds, making two cities. In attachment there are the well-delighted world and the teacher-disciple city, and in the pair of knowledge and limited agency there are further worlds.

[tal-a08-v422] World after world is set out, including the three sheath-cities, the city of speech, and the city of measure. Thus vidyā, together with the seven tattvas beginning with puruṣa, contains twenty-seven cities.

[tal-a08-v423] In the pure domain are Vāmeśa, Rūpa, and Sūkṣma; then pure knowledge and the measure of Śakti’s radiance; then Suviśuddhi and Śiva, and the worlds named Mokṣa, Dhuva, Īśa, Saṃbuddha, Samaya, and Sauśiva.

[tal-a08-v424] The peaceful level has seventeen cities. It includes the three cities of the Vidyeśas and Sadāśiva, the principles Bindu, Half-moon, and Nirodhikā, and reaches up to the supreme Sauśiva and the Indhikā and other cities of the central channel.

[tal-a08-v425] There are the supreme sound, the cavity of Brahman, the upper Kuṇḍalinī joined with Sūkṣma and others, and Śakti; then come five cities supported by Vyāpin, Vyoman, Ananta, and Anātha.

[tal-a08-v426] Then there is a sixth, supported by Paramamanas. Alternatively, one may speak of the sixteen-world group of Samanā, or of the enclosure of Bindu, the supreme Sauśiva, and the five worlds beginning with Indhikā.

[tal-a08-v427] The central-channel domain, the cavity of Brahman, Kuṇḍalinī, the five Vyāpins, and Samanā together make up this sixteen-world group. This is the pair of tattvas belonging to the level beyond peace.

[tal-a08-v428] In the revered Mataṅga scripture this sequence of cities is given: beginning with Kālāgni and the hells, it amounts principally to one hundred and forty.

[tal-a08-v429] Kūṣmāṇḍa, the seven netherworlds, the seven worlds, and Maheśvara make up the middle of the cosmic egg. Outside that, a hundred Rudras are situated.

[tal-a08-v430] There is a level of two hundred places joined with fifty-seven more. From the middle of a group of five eights, thirty-two are assigned within the four elements.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-niyatau śaṅkaradaśakaṃ kāle śivadaśakamiti puradvitayam / rāge suhṛṣṭabhuvanaṃ guruśiṣyapuraṃ ca vitkalāyugale bhuvanaṃ bhuvanaṃ niśi puṭapuratrayaṃ vākpuraṃ pramāṇapuram / iti saptaviṃśatipurā vidyā puruṣāditattvasaptakayuk vāmeśarūpasūkṣmaṃ śuddhaṃ vidyātha śaktitejasvimitiḥ / suviśuddhiśivau mokṣa dhuveṣisaṃbuddhasamayasauśivasaṃjñāḥ saptadaśapurā śāntā vidyeśasadāśivapuratritayayuktā / bindvardhendunirodhyaḥ parasauśivamindhikādipurasauṣumne paranādo brahmabilaṃ sūkṣmādiyutordhvakuṇḍalī śaktiḥ / vyāpivyomānantānāthānāśritapurāṇi pañca tataḥ ṣaṣṭhaṃ ca paramamanāśritamatha samanābhuvanaṣoḍaśī yadi vā / bindvāvaraṇaṃ parasauśivaṃ ca pañcendhikādibhuvanāni sauṣumnaṃ brahmabilaṃ kuṇḍalinī vyāpipañcakaṃ samanā / iti ṣoḍaśabhuvaneyaṃ tattvayugaṃ śāntyatītā syāt śrīmanmataṅgaśāstre ca kramo@yaṃ purapūgagaḥ / kālāgnirnarakāḥ khābdhiyutaṃ mukhyatayā śatam kūṣmāṇḍaḥ saptapātālī saptalokī maheśvaraḥ / ityaṇḍamadhyaṃ tadbāhye śataṃ rudrā iti sthitāḥ sthānānāṃ dviśatī bhūmiḥ saptapañcāśatā yutā / pañcāṣṭakasya madhyāddvātriṃśadbhūtacatuṣṭaye

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v431] In the subtle elements there are five, and there are the Viśvedevas and then a group of eight. A fifth grouping is connected with the senses, egoity, intellect, and the guṇas, including a group of eight gods.

[tal-a08-v432] In the root there is a group of eight yogas called Krodha, associated with time and with niyati. Patadruga and others, and Aṅguṣṭhamātra and others, belong to the tattva of attachment.

[tal-a08-v433] In vidyā there are twelve lords beginning with Ekaśiva, and in kalā there are ten. There is also a group of three hundred beginning with Vāmā, described by a numerical formula.

[tal-a08-v434] Some Śaiva beings up to this point are summarized as belonging to Śrīkaṇṭha. When someone desires the enjoyments of others, the appropriate application should be made there.

[tal-a08-v435] When something is removed, purification should be done, and the rest should be treated as included within. This is shown as a scriptural variant set forth for that purpose.

[tal-a08-v436] Teachers may also work out many other variants by their own understanding. In the revered former scripture, however, a count of one hundred and eighteen is stated.

[tal-a08-v437] Here the text briefly states the chief matters to be purified. The list begins with Kālāgni, Kūṣmāṇḍa, Narakeśa, Hāṭaka, and Bhūtalapa.

[tal-a08-v438] The list continues with Brahmā, the lord of the sage-world, and Rudras stationed in five intermediate regions. In the lower Ananta and in the east are those named Kapāli, Vahni, Anta, Nirṛti, and Bala.

[tal-a08-v439] The sequence runs upward through the named lords as far as Śambhu, together with the lord of Vīrabhadra. In the outer division of the Brahmāṇḍa there are eleven, and likewise five in the intermediate division.

[tal-a08-v440] Thus this group of sixteen cities is to be considered in nivṛtti and kalā. The list begins with Lakulīśa, Bhārabhūti, Diṇḍi, Āṣāḍhi, Puṣkara, and Nimeṣa.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-tanmātreṣu ca pañca syurviśvedevāstato@ṣṭakam / pañcamaṃ sendriye garve buddhau devāṣṭakaṃ guṇe yogāṣṭakaṃ krodhasaṃjñaṃ mūle kāle sanaiyate / patadrugādyāścāṅguṣṭhamātrādyā rāgatattvagāḥ dvādaśaikaśivādyāḥ syurvidyāyāṃ kalane daśa / vāmādyāstriśatī seyaṃ triparvaṇyabdhirasyayuk śaivāḥ kecidihānantāḥ śraikaṇṭhā iti saṃgrahaḥ / yatra yadā parabhogān bubhukṣate tatra yojanaṃ kāryam śodhanamatha taddhānau śeṣaṃ tvantargataṃ kāryam / ityāgamaṃ prathayituṃ darśitametadvikalpitaṃ tena anye@pi bahuvikalpāḥ svadhiyācāryaiḥ samabhyūhyāḥ / śrīpūrvaśāsane punaraṣṭādaśādhikaṃ śataṃ kathitam tadiha pradhānamadhikaṃ saṃkṣepeṇocyate śodhyam / kālāgniḥ kūṣmāṇḍo narakeśo hāṭako@tha bhūtalapaḥ brahmā munilokeśo rudrāḥ pañcāntarālasthāḥ / adhare@nantaḥ prācyāḥ kapālivahnyantanirṛtibalākhyāḥ laghunidhipatividyādhipaśambhūrdhvāntaṃ savīrabhadrapati / ekādaśabhirbāhye brahmāṇḍaṃ pañcabhistathāntarikaiḥ iti ṣoḍaśapurametannivṛttikalayeha kalanīyam / lakulīśabhārabhūtī diṇḍyāṣāḍhī ca puṣkaranimeṣau

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v441] In the water principle, Prabhāsa and Sureśa are present for each self together with their retinues, along with Bhairava, Kedāra, Mahākāla, Madhyāmra, and Jalpa.

[tal-a08-v442] In the principle of radiance is this secret group of eight: Śrīśaila, Hariścandra, and those named Bhīma, Indra, Aṭṭahāsa, Vimala, Kanakhala, Nakhala, Kuru, Sthita, and Gayā.

[tal-a08-v443] This most secret group of eight is associated with wind, with the tanmātras, and with the witness. Its members include Sthāṇu, Suvarṇa, Bhadra, Gokarṇaka, and Mahālayaka.

[tal-a08-v444] Avimukta, Rudrakoṭi, and Vastrāpada complete that pure group. In space are Sthūla, Sthūleśa, Śaṅku, Śruti, Kālañjara, and the bearer of the circle.

[tal-a08-v445] In the ego-principle there is a group of eight including Mākoṭa, the two Aṇḍas, and Chagalāṇḍa. Others also say that the tanmātras and the senses extend up to ahaṅkāra.

[tal-a08-v446] In intellect the group of eight sources is taught, and in primal nature the group of eight yogas beginning with Akṛta. Thus the established order consists of seven groups of eight worlds, extending from water up to the root.

[tal-a08-v447] In the human principle are Vāma, Bhīma, Ugra, Bhaveśa, Vīra, Pracaṇḍa, Gaurīśa, Aja, Ananta, and Ekaśiva. In vidyā there is the pair Krodha and Caṇḍa.

[tal-a08-v448] In kalā and niyati are Saṃvarta and Jyotiratha, and also Sūra and Pañcānta. In kāla is the triad named Vīra, Śikhīśa, and Śrīkaṇṭha.

[tal-a08-v449] These eight, led by Bhuvaneśa, are situated in the night division and in the thumb: Vāma with Mahātejā, Bhavodbhava, Ekapinga, Īśāna, and the rest of that group.

[tal-a08-v450] Vidyā has twenty-eight worlds, extending from puruṣa to the end of night. There are Hālāhala, Rudra, Krud, Ambikā, Aghorikā, and Vāmā.
chunks.sanskrit: [and]-prabhāsasureśāviti salile pratyātmakaṃ saparivāre / bhairavakedāramahākālā madhyāmrajalpākhyāḥ śrīśailahariścandrāviti guhyāṣṭakamidaṃ mahasi / bhīmendrāṭṭahāsavimalakanakhalanākhalakurusthitigayākhyāḥ atiguhyāṣṭakametanmaruti ca satanmātrake ca sākṣe ca / sthāṇusuvarṇākhyau kila bhadro gokarṇako mahālayakaḥ avimuktarudrakoṭī vastrāpada ityadaḥ pavitraṃ khe / sthūlasthūleśaśaṅkuśrutikālañjarāśca maṇḍalabhṛt mākoṭāṇḍadvitayacchagalāṇḍā aṣṭakaṃ hyahaṅkāre / anye@haṅkārāntastanmātrāṇīndriyāṇi cāpyāhuḥ dhiyi yonyaṣṭakamuktaṃ prakṛtau yogāṣṭakaṃ kilākṛtaprabhṛti / iti saptāṣṭakabhuvanā pratiṣṭhitiḥ salilato hi mūlāntā nari vāmo bhīmograu bhaveśavīrāḥ pracaṇḍagaurīśau / ajasānantaikaśivau vidyāyāṃ krodhacaṇḍayugmaṃ syāt saṃvarto jyotiratho kalāniyatyāṃ ca sūrapañcāntau / vīraśikhīśaśrīkaṇṭhasaṃjñametattrayaṃ ca kāle syāt samahātejā vāmo bhavodbhavaścaikapiṅgaleśānau / bhuvaneśapuraḥsarakāvaṅguṣṭha ime niśi sthitā hyaṣṭau aṣṭāviṃśatibhuvanā vidyā puruṣānniśāntamiyam / hālāhalarudrakrudambikāghorikāḥ savāmāḥ syuḥ

chunks.l2:
[tal-a08-v451] In vidyā are the Vidyeśvaras, and in Īśa there are eight. In Sadāśiva there are five: Vāmā, Jyeṣṭhā, Raudrī, Śakti, and Sakalā. This is the peaceful level.

[tal-a08-v452] Śāntyatītā consists of eighteen worlds, yet it is also itself a world. Thus the division of the path of space has been told, as instructed by revered Śambhu.
